Memoradums made by Henry B Jones of White Hall, Rockbridge County Va. continued from Vols 1&2 Cultivator.

p.desc: The winter of 1841&2 will be memorable for its mildness, there being very little severe freezing, & no ice put up in our state worth naming. After the mild winter there was considerable frost in April destroying the fruit in many places owing no doubt to the tender state of their bud.

body.p: The small grain looks very promising & heavy crops of wheat may be expected from present appearances. My crop is well set & I anticipate a better harvest than I have had this 7 years. Where I have limed my land the wheat is decidely superior to other parts of the farm.

In taking a survey of my business generally, it is in a better condition than since I purchased my land in 1834. I now flatter myself I shall be able to make a little something off my farm, hereforeto I have been a constant drain my purse in consequence of building Stylized Hs - possibly indicating a specific building.HH. Having completed my farming arrangements generally, & put off all necessary building good Hog pens & stable yards, I hope to realize something from an expenditure of little short of $10,000 in last 8 years.

My family is yet small, Whites Mrs. Jones, son Willie, niece Fanny Wright, & self Black, Sarah 50, & her daughter Abbey 11, Hetty 34 & her 3 children Catherine 6, Mariah 3 & Joe 1, Boy Jerry 17, & hired man Bob.

Have cut small lot clover hay which is good, grass generally short, corn is also short & much infested with worms. Not more than from 4-6 inches high but generally clearn & in good order rye is nearly ready to cut, & is a tolerable cross wheat is very good where well put in & on good land, & some maybe cut by the 22nd. The crop of apples is short, with some few peaches. Strawberry & cherrys abundant. were it not for the great indebtedness of the people, there would be good cuase to bless God for the may blessings we enjoy. Many are however sorely pressed, in the midst of abundace, to great scarcity of money, which has prevailed for the last year. We gave generally been bad economists for several years past, getting in debt beyond our means to pay & now while we abound in corn, wheat, & other grains at far prices with a super abundance of Meats of every kind, there is still much distress with many in the upper part of our county, on of debts which are pressed by executions & I have noticed sometihng like 100 horses posted up for public sale at our next July court, a fact unprecedented in the annal of our county - corn is (?) worth 40 to 50C oats 30c to 2p rye 4p wheat 6p flour $5- Bacon at home 8to 9C in the cities from 1/- to 8 beef on foot $4 sheep 6p to 9p per head with little or no demand for anything particularly where chas is regresed.

30th My 33°. Windy. Jerry still quite unwell. Will hire Crouses negroes
to day. 31st My 26°.
January 1st 1843
Mercury 20°. Clear fine morning. Jerry still very sick.
The winter up to this time has been cold but open, and favorable
to business. My stock of Every kind in fair order
& supplies for winter quite as good as usual.
My God watch over us & direct us in all things, for his
glory & or good. We would acknowledge his good^ness during the
past year & pray that we may so live as to merit a continuance
of Gods favour.
Monday 2nd My 28°. went to court, pd R.P. Baldwin $2.50 for paper
from 12th Augt 1842 to 12th Augt 1843. also pd G.W. White $8.75 in full
as Book in trade of sulkies with Ristine. Gave Patsy Porter $5.
Tuesday 3rd Clear windy morning My 27°. Jerry says he is
some better. (4th) cold morning My 16°. (5th) My 28° (6th) My 30°
7th Mercury 42° Cloudy warm morning. Jerry is better.
Sunday 8th Mercury 62°. Storm rain from the south with
very high wind & frost out on South sides. day fine &
clear. sermon by Revd Morrison
9th Mercury 34°. (10th) My 40°. rainy dark morning. Great fall
of rain to day from 12 to 1/2 past 2. Waters very full, & ground
much washed.
11th Mercury 34°. mending fences washed by flood. Jerry able
to sit up & Eat a little. 12th My 37°.
January
1843 Friday 13th Mercery 36°. Cloudy dark weather
Geo W. White, & Cousin Annn E Houston, married last Evening,
14th Mercury 20° 7 young persons spent night with uniform singing.
Betty Wright & Buck arrived from Waynesboro'
15th My 34°. Sermon by Revd Morrison John Nevins jr died yesterday
& buried to day at New Providence. up to 25th Feby 4 deaaths in
this family. J. Nevins sr & Jr & 2 black women.
Monday 16th. Mercury 33°. Fine morning. dined with sister i
company with Mrs. Beard & others.
17th My 32°. Spent day at Mr. Withrows. (18th) My 32°. (19th) My 33
20th My 37°. 21st Mercury 44°. Fine warm morning. Weather fine for 10 days
Sunday 22nd Mercury 54°. warm clear morning, sermon by Rvd Morrison.
23rd My 46°. (24th) Mercury 45°. James Withrow goes again West.
25th Mercury 37°. Very high wind for 2 nights & still blowing.
26th My 31°. calm morning. 3 Lambs. (27th) My 38° 28th My 43°
Sunday 29th Mercury 31°. sermon by Revd Js. Morrison. (30th) My 30°
31st Mercury 34°. Slight fall snow. 6 Lambs to date.
February 1st. Cold windy morning. My 19°. (2nd) My 10°. Clearned up
2/4 Bushels clover seed worth 4$ 70 Bushel. 3rd My 24°. (4th) My 28°
Sunday 5th My 32°. Snowed abt 3 Inches last night. Sermon by Revd Morrison
6th cold windy night My 18°. will go to court - very
windy cold night Mercury not above 21°. during the day
7th wind still blowing My dow to 8°.
Wednesday 8th Mercury 9°. Calm morning. Severe freezing since 5th. Just.
9th My 27°. Revd Morrisons examination at school house & singing.
fine turn out of young persons near 100 of singing. 8 or 10 with us.
Friday 10th Mercury 25°. cloudy with little rain (11th) Mercury 39°. windy
12th My 40°. good sermon by Revd Morrison (13th) My 31°. cash Chapman $3D
14th Mercury 29°. Splitting rails & hawling logs on (13th) (15th) My 31°. rain & sleet
16th very cold again, My 12°. clear & windy. Recd 2 Tons plaster from
Scottsville by Tate Wallace, at $5 p Ton cauniage (?). Attended Wa. Ths Newton
Willsons School examination; The children acquitted themselves
with great credit. & W. Willson is a most excellent Teacher & estimable man
Friday 17th My 22°. (18th) My 24°. (19th) My 38°. (20th) My 42°. (21st) My 31°. (22nd) My 33 Mr
John Nevins Sr buried to day. Friend Trimble with us last night
23rd My 26°. (24th) My 32°. 3 In. snow. 25th My 33°. sowed 3/2 Bushels clover seed.
1843 February 26th. Sunday fine bright frosty morning. My 30°
sick list rather better, There is considerable sicness in the neighborhood.
Many children companing of Billious ammonia, & several families
down with fiver. & very bad colds in almost Every family. The winter
has been pretty cold without much snow. Small grain looks badly &
clover much frozen out. My stock looks generally well. supply fair.
Monday 27th My 46°. Windy & fair. Clearing off N.E. Hill field for oats.
28th Mercury 31°. cloudy snowed 3 or 4 Inches. sent by mail to B & Burtoor 6/-
March 1st Windy frosty morning. Mercury 26°. Snow abt 3 Inches deep.
2nd. Snow gone on South side. very cold windy morning, My 18°.
3rd cold morning. Mercury down to 12°. cold weather for March.
4th My 23°. cloudy. (5th) East wind, with snow, My 24°. sermon by Rd Mn
6th still cold, My 16°. clear, will go to court. collected from
W. Taylor $62.44 & paid Hy. A. McCormick $30 & John Ritchie
$22. & Lo and Majr I. Stuart $3 paid Bear fro Repair watch $2.50
7th Mercury 19°. paid T. N. Wilson $4.50 Tuition feeds in full
paid Majr Brooks 1$ for Mrs. Gibbs salary. 8th My 24°
9th Mercury 34°. Waggon will go for Collierstown to day send
cash for flax send $40. fixed up furnace pd Kisters on 3p in full.
Friday 10th Mercury 36°. Foggy. with some rain waggon returned with
flax seed 10 at night. 41 Bushels. due Harber & Leach $4.06 McCorkle
& @ [all] $9.06 payable in April. singing & examination & school House
A calf from Margretta Bull.
11th Fine morning Mercury 39°. Fixed up shed & calf stable & cow stalls
12th Sunday, cold raw morning, with East wind My 30°. Hazy.
sermon by Revd Morrison, snow in Evening inch deep
13th still cloudy. My 29°. fixed up colt stables. changeable day.
14th cold morning, My 19°. 15th Mercury 38°. windy will
15th commence plowing for oats to day. ground still
much frozen on North sides. Backward spring - a calf from Hariss
16th Mercur 25°. cold East wind, with skiff of snow. continued
cold & snowing all day. My down to 25°. at noon. Snow 6 In.
Br. James Withrow returned from St. Charles
17th My 23°. snow clouds & cold wind. Will take a slay ride to visit
sister Caroline. Rented house of Dr. Jines to Dr. Morgan.
Saturday 18th March 1843. Mercury 14°. Spent day at Pas [?]
Brother Samuels & Girls & Willie at Mr. Beards singing, bring the
last day. paid him in full. D. $.50¢. Slaying still good.
Sunday 19th Mercury 13 1/2°. Hazy winter weather, snow but little
melted. No preaching to day. 20th My 10°. Truly cold weather.
21st My 22°. Still cloudy & cold. Hawling out rails to make & repair fences
22nd My 20°. Hazy after a beautiful clear night. still at rails for S E fence
23rd Very cold My 10°. Hight wind, with clear sky. after a week of coudy
weather. ground still mostly covered with snow. Mercury at noon 18°.
Mercury at sun set 14°. H.E. Wright left for Waynesboro' to day.
Friday 24th Mercury 10°. This is unexampled weather for March so far
as any memory goes. Windy & fair.
25th My 23°. Will go to otwn to hands to fix Dr. Hines house & stable
26th Clear & Cold with windy, My 28°. Sermon by Revd Morrison.
Gave 6p to Education Society. cool day, with East wind.
Monday 27th Mercury 29°. Spitting snow. Will bring some manure
from Brownsburg to day. & finish fixng Dr. Hines stable.
28th Mercury 36°. rained a good deal during the night & still
raining. Will go to day to appraise property at J. Nevins.
Wednesday Fair, frosty & windy My 27°. Waters pretty fresh sawing & H'z dry
30th My 34°. attended at Nevins Sale & bought 14 of Steele for 7/6
old irons 63¢ apple mill $2.00 mould Board 6p flax Brake 36¢
plow 65¢ long Ladders 40c/ Bee hives $2.12 ¢ Sledge 1.15 & pd
cash for 8 hogs heads 7/6 other property due in 12 months
property sold well generally. ($9.58 in all) $8.33
Friday 31st My 40°. Cloudy, a wet warm unpleasant day, brought
home articles from Nevins, 13~ cash of Chapman $40. 5 pigs
from Sally pig.
April 1st My 45°. Fine spring morning, warm & fair.
put up fence from orchard to the mill & enlarged orchard. also
fixed up Bee bunch & will try my luck with Honey.
Sunday 2nd My 28°. clear & cool. sermon by Revd AD Metcalf
3rd My 34° slight snow. will go to court. pd Harper $4 Dr.
McCorkle $9 - Dr Wade $14. H pd McCormick in all $8.
April 4th My 33°. 2 or 3 Inches Snow, ground very wet
5th My 35°. Still snow (6th) Mercury 36°. snow mostly gone
7th My 32°. plowing again. (8th) My 50°. Cloudy. planted potatoes
and little Early corn, sowed cabbage & radish seed
Sunday 9th Mercury 48°. snow showers, Sermon by Revd Morrison
10th My 35°. North Mountain covered with snow.
11th My 34°. plnated peas, set out onions, sowed cabbage & Lettuce
12th Mercury 48°. 13th Mercury 46°. rainy day with thunder
sowed some planter, & cleaned up some 50 bushels flax seed
14th Mercury 52°. still cloudy after much rain last night
Waters quite fresh
15th Mercury 45°. Fine morning with dew. finished fence
to near School house spring with cedar & Locust posts also fence
across to Wards line from corner of lower orchard
Sunday 16th Mercury 34°. Cloudy with some rain Sermon by Rd M
17th Mercury 56°. will go to court to day as witness in case of
Bedsen(?). will send abt 100 Gallons oil to Richd by J. Brownlee
made fence for Margaret Poague. Mr. Brownlee returned & unloaded
18th sowing plaster & pruning trees. Much thunder, & rain last
Night. My 55°. rain again at 2 P.M. (19th) cloudy My 44°.
Thursday 20th. Mercury 46°. still cloudy, sowing oats &
spring wheat 2 Bushels S.W. & 10 of oats
21st My 45°. sowing clover seed on oats ground 1 1/4 Bushels sown
22nd My 55°. growing weather. sowed 1/2 Bu[shel] flax seed.
which ought to heave been sown last week.
Grafteed a number of young fruit trees this week
with Bell flower, sick no further, winter sweating
Rombo with Sunday pears, plumbs & @ [all]
Sunday 23rd My 60°. Revd Morrison absent Mossy Creek Presbytery.
24th Mercury 65°. Hawling manure & Rails - 25th My 57°.
26th still fine weather, My 53 commenced plowing for
corn, when I should be planting.
27th My 61°. fine growing Weather, Election day, Stuart Congress
Peyton Senate Moore Apembey White Lackey Caruthers
Friday 28th April 1843 Fine morning, My 44°.
Grafting large apple Tree at Barn, leaves beginning to show
Peach trees in Beautiful & full bloom & forest trees are
beginning to bud
29th still fine weather, My 48°. Finished covering my
Spring house wto day with different grades of shingles
some thin some thick, some black oak on the top
made from timber in the sap state, cut in M.L.
some apple trees in bloom, dog wood not yet out.
Sunday 30th Mercury 58°. cloudy with rain Sunday school to
commence to day.
May 1st Mercury 49°. windy. cool morning. 2nd My 42°.
3rd My 49°. raining. 4th My 48°. 5th planted melon seed
6th My 57°. ready to plant corn after 2 weeks hard work.
Sunday 7th Mercury 63°. sermons by Revd Morrison showry day.
8th My 61°. commenced planting corn planted 1/2 Bushels on abt 13 acrs
9th My 57°. finished planting in field bought off Ward & new ground.
have yet some lots to plant & orchard East of the house.
Easterly storm commenced this afternoon, a good rain.
Monday 10th still raining & blowing from the Est. My 48°. (11th) My 48°
12th Mercury 52°. plowing orchard for corn 13th My 50°.
Sunday 14th Mercury 34°. No preaching to day at N.P. No. S. School
15th warm morning. My 66°. rain & much thunder & Lightening at (?)
16th My 68°. Miss R. Willson married to Mr. Stirrett. Delightful morning.
put rafters & Laths on workshop shed. now ready for shingling
17th Mercury 55°. still fine growing weather. sheering sheep &
working on raod. Evening rain.
Thursday 18th Mercury 50°. still raining. wind East. (19th) My 46°. cloudy
20th My 47°. fine day p[l]anted 10 bu[shels] potatoes, new ground 2
more will finish the patch By cash Brownlee for oil sold $30.
Whole bill $85.
Sunday 21st My 44°. fine morning. 50 scholars at S. School, sermon by W.Mr
Morrison.
Monday 22nd My 50°. Mrs. Jones bought goods at amt $21 -pd cash
put on shed roof at work shop.
1843 May 23rd Growing weather, Mercury 48°. planting potatoes
24th Mercury 55°. Fine morning. still planting potatoes & arranging stock.
25th My 48°. Gent muster day. By cash Kirkpatrick $12.75 Dr. Stuart $3-
pd D. Brown for Hat $4~ Killed small calf 140 lb.
26th Mercury 59°. Sacramental season commences to day Mr. Ewing
with us. 27th My 62°. fine morning repairing dam, & hawling rock.
28th Mercury 55°. Hazy. fine congregation, rain in evening.
29th Raining, Mercury 62°. growing weather. Evening, much rain & wind
30th Hazy cool morning Mercury 44°. (31st) My 57°.
June 1st. Cool morning. fair with slight frost Mercury 42°.
2nd Mercury 41°. 3rd My 60°. Loaded waggon with oil 200
gallons, & 700 o Butter for Richd. Margaret Beard left for house.
Sunday 4th My 56°. fine morning ^5th My 68° went to court. Collected $150 from
Geo Swoope & paid out same to Jos. W. Culton $50. Patsy Porter
$50 & H A McCormick $50 also pd $2. Subscription to build
Bethesda Church. started waggon to Richd with oil & butter.
Tuesday 6th warm morning. My 68°. high wind in the night
will set out for Richd this morning.
Friday 17th Mercury 62°. Returned from Richd last evening. had a
very pleasant trip, a bought a good stock of goods. groceries
& @ [all] Sold 184 p Gallons oil for 5/3 p Gallon butter for $3.08. &
2 bunches feathers for $10. in all $174.51 I paid for good brown
sugar $6 1/2 coffee 8 to $9 Loaf sugar 12 p $ 2 a 6p molases 2p fish
herring $4 1/2 Not (?) shad $7 1/4 Tar 1.63 Trains oil $13. Dry goods
are generally very lower paid A Patterson $2 for 4 old barrels on 19th
18th Mercury 66° Some rain last night, the weather is now
quite seasonable. Fine rain to day.
Sunday 19th My 56°. about 50 scholars at Sabbath school
19th May 58°. delivered goods in Brownsburg. Load worth abt $40
20th My 56° (21st) My 57°. commenced cutting clover hay.
22nd My 62°. Have been unwell for 2 days, better to day.
24th My 66°. hawling in hay, put up 8 loads nice hay to day
paid Mr Soniley(?) for 3 days mowing 3/9 p Day.
1843 Sunday 25th June. Hazy morning, My 62°.
Sermon by Revd Morrison
26th Mercury 65° close morning, with thunder. put up 2
loads hay in all to date about 10 Tons.
27th Mercury 65°. Heavy atmosphere, sleight rain in Evening.
28th Cloudy, My 67°. Cherries ripe, also rasberries & currents.
29th My 64°. Fair & getting dry (30th) My 67° Bees swarmed.
July 1st. Warm morning My 68°. Harvest beginning.
Wheat ripens slowly & will not be fit to cut before
4th to 6th Jnst. crop has improved but will fall
sar short of a good one. Many fields rusted. &
few that are not too thing on the ground.
This day has been very warm Mercury rose to 92°. the
past week warm & dry varying from 86° to 90°.
2nd Mercury 71°. still clear & Dry - rain at noon a good
shower. with much thunder & @ [all] seromon by Revd S. Brown.
3rd Cool morning. My 56°. 4th Fine morning, My 52°. cool.
5th Hazy My 59°. Mowing in Meadow. Danl helping to day.
6th Mercury 66°. Cloudy & windy. Still at hay. Put up 70 cocks
7th Mercury 62°. Still hazy without rain. ground getting very dry.
will commence cutting wheat to day, which ripens
slowly, meadon abt half cut.
July 8th My 70° still cutting wheat & putting up hay. Wheat
generally not ready to cut. Most farmers in this
neighborhood will begin on Monday 10th. My
wheat is quite an average crop for the ground
[?} is on, & of fine generally of grain - put up 10
day 7 lods hay in good order. in all to date 17
loads. Daniel helped to mow & harvest 2/3 days this week
gave to hime our order Dr Mooney for $2. paid
Nicholas cash 6; Due Nutty 75 cents for work in
harvest & hay making.
Sunday 9th My 64°. Sermon by Revd Morrison.
July 10th 1843 Mercury 66°. Cutting some clover hay
which is fill ripe. Wheat harvest commenced
generally, the crop is rusted & well not be over 2/3rd
of a crop at most.
11th Mercury 68°. Still working at hay. Mrs. Jones weaning little
son John Henry Bawzwell who will be one year old on 19th Just.
12th Dark cloudy weather will but little rain, My 66°. cleaning
potatoes & melon patches.
13th still cloudy with but little rain, My 65°. cutting wheat.
14th Mercury 68°. Mrs. Jones, Sister Caroline, James Withrow &
the children set out for Waynesboro at 7 A.M. Cut wheat
till 12. Made 4 loads hay in the Evening. hauled in 2.
15th May 66°. fine morning. warm day. apricots in fine Eating
order. Nut meg peaches getting ripe and several apple
trees dropping fruit whichi s pretty good. also some
pears fit to eat.
16th Mercury 70°. warm day & much rain & thunder North & East
none here. Sermon by Revd McCorkle & Morrison.
17th Clear fine morning, My 66°. 18th My 70°. finished harvesting
at 10 A.M. pulled flax to day. Mrs. Jones & @ [all] returned home.
19th Mercury 66°. Boys at Mucks. Recd cash of Ro. McCormick 14$
sent Wm Houston $50 by George W. Houston - 20th my 64°. Pleasant day.
21st Cool morning. Mercury 57°. Fair & Dry. Hawling in wheat.
22nd My 51°. Cash of Swoope $60- Cutting oats & making hay
paid Daniel Cash 6/~
23rd Mercury 58°. 24th My 61°. (25th) Mercury 64°. Sent
through A Patterson $4 to pay for Post up to 27th Jany.
1844 present A Carson & Mr. Withrow. Mrs. Morgan & Cadie
to see us to day.
26th Mercury 70°. corn suffering much for want of rain
there has been but little rain for a month.
29th My 68°. (28th) My 68° will thrash wheat to day. 29th My 70°
Mrs. Beard with us. Put up last of my heay in Cock, the crop
has been very good, second above 30 Tons.
1843 July 30th Sunday, warm & very dry, garden
Suffering very much, and corn greatly injured & without
rain in a few days must be a very short crop in
this neighbourhood 4 PM a good rain. Sermon by
Revd M.C. Roy. Gave 6/~ to VA Bible Society.
31st Mercury 71°. Raining moderately with East wind.
continued to rain till noon, ground is now wet, thanks
to Almight God for this great blessing - Mrs. Jones &
Mrs Beard went to Mrs. McNuts.
August 1st. Mercury 50°. Cleaning up wheat. Spent day at
Squire McNuts. 2nd My 58°. Mr. Links sons with us.
3rd My 60°. Fine growing weather. will go to court.
collected $14.57 of Q.D. Davidson.
4th My 65°. Mrs. Hy Brown Miss McNut & 3 Mrs Withrows visit us
to day also Mr. Rick McNut. MissLinks left this morning,
Clearned up to day 23 Bushels G.S. wheat for sure
also 21 Dc Flint. Cleaned on tuesday 118 Bushels wheat
in all 162 Bushels, Have of screenings abt 30
bushels - have my spring wheat got to thrash
Finished putting up my oats abt 180 bushels.
& have put away in good order upwards of 30 Tons
of hay. Every thing snug & nice for the season, and
all in good health. For which I Thank God.
5th Mercury 63°. Cloudy for last 30 hours with East wind & a
little rain. Uncle Archd Withrow died suddenly yesterday.
6th My 66°. Fair. sermon by Revd Morrison. (7th) My 70°. sow Turnip
seed to day. (8th) My 67°. Commenced plowing to day for
rye. paid James Mooney infull $5.50
9th My 66°. raining. (10th) cloudy My 65°. Waters low, but the
weather is tolerably seasonable. Cleaning of hill
for wheat. Next Palmers. a son born to Mrs. Helen Withrow
11th My 62°. Fine morning. (12th) My 62°. a shower last
evening. Mr. J.B. Greene put clock in order pd off He is
to be a long in 12 or 13 months. M.F. Wright on a visit
to Waynesboro.
1843 Sunday August 13th. Mercury 61°. with fog & heavy dust.
sermon by Revd Morrison. Elders Brooks Culton & Withrow ordained.
Monday 14th My 63°. John E. Beard on a visit to us. 15th My 64°
paid Daniel $2 & setled all assets to date. peaches getting ripe.
16th My 64°. (17th) My 64°. (18th) My 64°. Sacramental season Revd Thomas
& McFarland present. Fanny, Emma & Cremond arrived from
Wayensboro. (19th) My 67°. sermons by Revd Thomas & McFarland,
A good rain in the Evening for which may God by praised.
Sunday 20th Mercury 65°. Damp morning. Moderate & good rain.
Sermons by Revd McFarland & Thomas.
Monday 21st. Mercury 62°. Fine weather, seeding up in bottoms next
the mile on which I will sow Timothy seed to make permanent
meadow. abt 1 Bushel Timothy seed sown.
22nd My 64°. 23rd My 66°. will go for Wayensborough
25th Returned from Wayensborough, settled partially our
business, Showing a ballance of $4,000 to $5,000 in my
favour besides a bond due for $2000. Should the debts
be all collected we will have done will, I however
clear a loss of some $12 to 1500$ $12 to $1500 Had a pleasant
trip than otherwise, but on my return home had a
very severe fall from my horse.
Saturday 26th Mercury 67°. weather very seasonable
fruit in good order for Eating. paid out $5. on Amy
Petross order. My neck still very stiff & sore.
Sunday 27th My 68°. Cloudy. Heavy rain to day. did not go to
church on a/c of my fall. Sermon by Revd Morrison.
28th My 68°. Cloudy damp weather. (29th) My 63°. Cloudy
30th Mercury 69°. fine morning. (31st) My 68°. clear fine weather.
September 1st. Fine seasonable weather, Mercury 68°.
2nd My 66°. Sent 2 Lambs to Colo Reid & will go for
iron and flax seed to Grove to day. 11 Bushels seed from
R.B. Anderson. & 1184 a Iron from Wm Davis, in Change for 600 [of] Bacon.
Sunday 3rd Sept 1843 Mercury 67°. Fine clear morning.
Mr. Morrison absent attending Presbytery at Union.
Monday 4th My 66°. Still fine fair weather & very seasonable.
5th My 66°. fair & fine warm weather. working at dam
6th 68° (7th) Mercury 67°. Much thunder & Lightening & rain
for several days past, with very warm weather for 10 days
Sent by Jerry 1184 a Iron to Mr. Withrow, Waynesboro to be
sold for $60~
Friday 8th My 68°. Repairing dam & cutting banks of the run
9th My 66°. Cousin Susan & S.H. Wayland up on a visit
also Mr. & Mrs. Payne & children. Mr. Gulley & family going to Louisburg, shortly
Sunday 10th My 58°. cool East wind. Dismissed Sunday school.
11th Raining, My 60°. quite an Easterly storm wind & rain.
12th My 57°. Still cloudy & cool. Made some cider
for peach butter. (13th) My 53°. Still cloudy disagreeable
weather, Boiling peach butter. finished same in
18th hours, or midnight, got about 12 Gallons butter from 30 of
Cider & 3 bushels of pealed peaches. More peaches would
have been better, & the cider should be boiled the day
previous, in which the peaches ought to be bursted at the
rate of 4 bushels to 30 Gallons of cider.
14th. wind still East with rain, Mercury 60°. continued
to rain through out the day & night, waters very high.
15th Mercury 68°. wind south, with some clear spots.
been cloudy & raining for last 5 days. sawed & mended dam.
16th. Mercury 60°. fine morning. Cousin Susan goes home to day.

p.note: Note added in pencil, "Slave. Hetty was the cook."
p.ref: Hetty gave birth to another son.

body.p: 17th Mercury 64°. Foggy morning. sermons by Revd Morrison.
fine weather for 3 days. Niece Betty Wright with us
for some days.
18th My 66°. will go to court to day. pd shiriff(?) $7.65 through
Colo Caruthers, paid James B Trimble, by son Wm $15. paid
Dunkum $2.25. he is due me 6/9. pd Jacob Dice for flax seed $12.
19th My 66°. Mrs Morrison, Maybury, & Houston spent the day with us.
Wednesday 20th September 1843 commenced sowing wheat
will so York Flint in field next Beards line, roled in ashes
& plaster, in proportion to one bushels to 2. Have sowed
8 bushels rye to date. 4 in bottom & 4 next Beards line, north. Mercury 67°. Weather very
warm for season mercury rising to 87° in heat of the
day. Sowed 4 Bushels which was plowed in (21st) Do 4. [illegible] 22nd 4 Do
12 Bushels shown in 1st Square, down from Persimon Tree, 23rd
sowed 6 Bushels, 26th & 27th sowed 5 Bushels plowed in, in all 23 bushels
of wheat $ 5 of rye.
Thursday 21st Mercury 72°. very warm for the season. 22nd My 66°
23rd Mercury 70°. Cloudy & warm.
Sunday 24th Mercury 67°. Season fine to date. Sermon by Revd
Morrison (25th) My 64°. (26) My 70°. storm of wind & rain.
27th Great change since yesterdays Thunder storm. wind
East, Mercury 52°. went to see Rea. settled with McCormick &
collected from him $8.88¢. settled note due to Mr. P. Rogers to Mr. Withrow
jr & @ [all] $74. 7 pigs from Berkshire
28th Mercury 50°. will vist Mr. Beards, Kerns, Cruk, will commence
cutting up corn to day. 30th Returned from Kerr Creek
Recd Cash of A. Withrow for oil $16.
Oct 1st. My 62°. Sermon by Revd Morrison. Gave 6/~ to U.T. Seminary
22nd My 61°. fine morning (3rd) My 56°. (4th) My 50°. Mr.
Lowman commenced work to day at $8 p month, still
cutting up corn. Danl quit work in the mill to day
& Jerry went in. Recd Cash Jas. Kelly $20. Pd Patterson & co $12.42
5th Mercury 41°. Slight frost the first This fall
Recd cash of Dhirl for oil $28.50 of Belly Johnston 9d
6th Fine weather My 45°. commenced seeding in
corn with 3 Tongues - sowed 3/2 Bu[shel] Golden Shuck wheat
7 My 63°. Cloudy. Seeded 2/~ bushels to day. corning, rain.
8th Mercury 53°. good rain last night. & Still raining.
sermon by Revd Morrison.
9th Mercury 43°. sowed 3 bushels wheat G.S.
10th My 44°. fine fall weather. finished Lot of wheat
down Coal pit down, 12 bushels seed sown.
11th Mercury 44°. Mrs. Brown & sister with us to day.
1843 October 12th Mercury 34°. The weather is still
very fine, Peaches mostly gone, one tree yet to
ripen paid Ths Paxton $15~ purchased Buck sheep off
Benjn Gregory.
13th My 37°. frost. (14th) My 34°. quite frosty. finished
seeding in corn ground. sowed on price got of waid 6
Bushels & Balance of the field 12 bushels. in all 18. Sixteen
of which is golden Shuck 2 white wheat got off M Nevins,
& twenty three bushels flint wheat sown next Palmers on
fallors lane.
15th Sunday Quite frosty morning My 33°. No preaching
to day. Mr. Morrison absent at Synod Lewisburg.
Monday 16th Mercury 37°. Finished cutting up corn, which
is quite a good crop for the ground out, supposed
at least 40 bushels p[er] acre on an average.
17th My 36°. will gather apples to day & put up
hogs to fatten. (18th) My 33°. 19th My 40°. paid James B
Trimble $27~ Recd cash H. Admans 3¢ pd Patterson
for cannisters & crocks $ @ [all] $2.00
20th my 40° (21st) My 50°. Loaded waggon for Richmond
with 10 Bbls extra flour, 60 Gallons oil for B&G Jones
11 p/~ for Mr. Withrow 5 for B.F. Graham, also 1 for kin
butter 58er 2/~ Bushel dried peaches. Load to Richd
worth about $125. Sent under care of John Lowman.
Sunday 22nd My 60°. warm fine morning. sermon
by Revd Morrison, evening, moderate rain.
Monday 23rd My 38°. Waggon started for Richd pave
Mr. Lowman $2. cash pd McGuffin for flax seed
$8.40 in order from Bryan ¢7 cash $1.40
24th My 34° Mowing 2nd rop hay which is good
25th My 50° raind a little last night & like for more
26th My 46° light rain, (27th) My 39°. a good rain last night
Saturday 28th Oct 1843 Mercury 31° Some ice, Sacramental
season, Preaching yesterday by Revd Payne
Sermons to day by Revd Love & McCutchrow, Eving Revd Payne
preached at school house to small congregation.
Sunday 29th Fine Frosty morning, My 32°. Miss Finley &
Payne with us. Revd Love preached to day assisted by Mr. Paxton
McCutchrow & Morrison Revd Love & Mr Donald & Miss Finley & Payne
to dinner with us. Weather fine for last few days.
Monday 30th Mercury 43°. raining moderately. evening fair.
31st Mercury 28°. quite frosty, ground frozed. shy hazy. digging
potatoes & putting up hay fall crop, very good. paid A.
Nevins 11/3 for 3 bu[shels] flax seed. Ground 30/~ flax seed.
November 1st Mercury 26°. frosty night, rain.
2nd My 44°. windy but pleasant. A heifer calf from Lilly.
3rd My 36°. Digging potatoes. 4th My 35°. spitting snow.
Sunday 5th Cloudy disagreeable morning, with cold East
wind, May 31°. sermon by Revd Morrison.
6th My 21°. will go to court to day. Mr. Lowman returned
from Richmond with 10 sacks salt, 175 20 bushels potatoes, 1 cheese
paid Mr. Lowman - $3.87/~ Returned from court late, done
little or no business.
7th My 37°. snowing (8th) My 34°. will fire coal pit to day
9th Mercury 26°. quite frosty. (10th) My 44°. little rain last night
Got of James Potter 25 flour barrels left at whites Mill pd for
same $7.50. Brought home from Pattersons 6/~ Bu[shelsl] good
flax seed 4/6 1 Do. bad at 0/6. of D. Brown 9 Bu[shels] at 4/~ left
with Patterson 3 sacks salt for sale & 12 Bu[shels] Potatoes of
5/3 p bushel. recd cash of box for Bacon & Potatoes 6/~
Hawled 9 loads wood to day. Mr. John Lowman
returned to day at 12 o clock.
11th My 55°. raining. cleared off at 10 after much rain & wind.
loaded waggon for Scottsville 112 Gall[ons]s oil, & 8 Bbls
flour,
Sunday 12th My 32°. windy night
1843 Nov. 14 Returned from Waynesboro left for
rocle. Recd cash Wm Withrow $30. weather been quite cold for
last 2 days.
15th Mercury 36°. fine morning. Hawled 315 Bushels
coal to Brownsburg 16th My 40° will go to the
Fair held at Lexington to day & Tomorrow.
17th Returned from Fair in the rain, exebition only
tolerable. Ladies department as usual the best.
paid Mr. C. Lewis $15 commissioners fee. Boys
finished hawling coal 5 Loads making good Bushels
18th Fine morning. clear Mercury 53°. Mr. Lowman
returned from Scottsville, sold oil 97 Gallons for 85¢
p[er] Gallon $82.45 & 8 Bbls flour at $4 - $32. Brought
home 1 Ton plaster. & 11 Bushels flax seed from
Mr. Withrow
Sunday 19th My 43° fine weather. sermon by Revd
Morrison.
20th My 37°. cloudy Eveni[n]g rain. 21st My 41°. Fair. Took 1
Tom plaster from Mr. Withrow to Pattersons Mill & one
from Scottsville yesterday. Have now 2 Tons these.
Recd cash of Mr. Withrow for my hog Billy $110-
Wednesday 22nd My 46°. 23rd my 38°. Mr. Lowman goes with
the waggon to day to move Mr. G.W. Jalley. worked 2 days
on road equal to $5.50 paid Taxes $22.50. & road levy $9 $31 1/2
24th Mercury 56°. Cloudy & warm.
Saturday 25th My 38°. fine morning. Made some cider,
& husked some corn, paid Nick 4¢ on a/c of
burning coal pit. also pd him for crade ni
sack of salt at $4. When he shall have
worked 12 days more I will owe him $3-
Saturday 26th My 36° Cloudy 27th Killed 12 hogs to day weighing
2440 ea smallest 150 largest 298° average abt 203 lb
Tuesday 28th Nov 1843 My 30° weighed 3 Hogs gross, one
with heavy coat of hair, that had run out till put up
to fatten weighed gross 290, nut 236 lb 54 lb Taro. one pnd
since April last, & will fed 310 lb gross Tare 40 lb, nut 270 lb
one ditto trated as the last, 340 lb gross Tare 42 lb nut 298 lb.
The first loosing less than one fifth, the two last abt our
seventh - on Cutting up my pork I find it very nice
& white it has been corn fed near 2 months & will
make very fine bacon.
Wednesday 29th My 38°. raining a little. 30th My 41°.
Finished hawling in my corn & am nearly ready for winter.
December 1st. Snowed last night abt 2 inches deep & still
hailing, rather gloomy for 1st of winter. Mercury 34°.
engaged in husking corn which happily is nearly all under
cover - Paid Mr. Brown $6 infull for flax seed &@ [all]
2nd Mercury 33°. Still cloudy. unpleasant weather for 2 days.
Sunday 3rd My 31°. Sermon by Revd Calhoun, fine bright day.
4th My 24°. Quite frosty, went to Court, paid J.D. Davidson
$34.37 infull on a/c M Chesneys Estate, Paid P. Trotter $5
infull as commissioner to settle Porters Estate.
5th My 34° windy night. (6th) My 20°. cloudy unpleasant day
7th Mercury 30°. raining, sleeting & snowing. picking Mill stones
to day Jerry & Mr. Talley assisting put part of my apples in
cellar & store room to day.
8th Mercury 30°. quite wintery weather. ground covered with
snow & sleet for several days. (9th) My 35°. 10th My 32°.
Sermon by Revd Metcalf. 11th My 40°. Thawing cloudy day
12st Fair, Mercury 33°. fixing up barn yard lots, preparatory
to yarding the cattle. Gass nearly gone in the meadow.
Wednesday 13th My 16°. Clear & cold, after windy night
put up cattle for winter quarters. (14th) My 20°.
hawled 9 loads wood, 15th My 35°. (16th) My warm &
cloudy Cousin Edwin Wayland spent night with us.
1843 December 17th Mercury 54°. warm rainy weather
for last 24 hours, have been afflicted with Eresipoles(?) for
last 4 days which is very painful, got bled & will take
a course salts. Collection taken up to day for domestic
missions, will send my dollar by Fanny & Willie.
Sermon by Revd Morrison
Monday 18th Mercry 35°. (19th) My 38°. Cloudy & soft weather.
My right arm above the elbow wrist broken out with about
1 doz biles & very painful for a week past
20th My 30°. foggy morning (21st) My 35°. 22nd My 41°. raining.
Mrs. Jones complaining a little, My arm running truly but
still very painful & much inflamed.
Saturday 23rd My 45°. Mrs. Jones taken unwell last night.
Doctr Gold sent for & arrived at 12. Had a fine daughter
born between 1 & 2 Oclock this morning. Mrs. Smith & Mrs.
Talley also with us. My own health inproving. Paid
Doctr Gold $50 Recd from Mr. Withrow by John Withrow
$63. on a/c of money due me at Scottsville.
Sunday 24th Mercury 38°. Foggy till 1 P.M. sermon by Revd
Morrison. Mrs. Jones continues quite as well as could
be expected. Little daughter weighs 8/4 lb
Christmas day Monday 25th Dec Family in pretty good
health. Mrs. Jones & little daughter, as well as is usual
in such cases. Mercury 34°. Some frost & quite
Foggy. Some /~ dozen Old Ladies, with Brother Samuel
dined with us to day.
26th Mercury 37°. Rather unremarkable weather for
the season, heavy fogs till noon for last 3 days.
will kill 8 hogs to day - Gross weight 1240 lb in all 3684 lb
27th My 45° Still warm fine weather. cutting up meat
28th Mercury 31°. fine frosty morning. paid Mrs. Crouse $20
29th windy night. My 32°. Mrs. Jones able to be up
a little. 30th My 26°. paid Mr. Brown Salary $8 Do Patterson $5. on a/c
McCormick (31st) My 32°.
1844 January 1st
It has pleased God in his infinite goodness to
spare our lives to the beginning of another year; we
have been greatly blessed in all things, in times past, and
we would now pour out our hearts in gratitude and
praise to God, who has kindly preserved us, and watch
over our destinies, who has continued unto us our lives
our helth & strength; and who had in all things
prospered us beyond our deserts. O God we would pray
thee stll to voicesafe unto our household they watchful
and kind providence; Grant that each one of us, may
through the influnces of they devide presence, live more
near to thee than we have hither to done. We would pray
for thy direction in all things. Fit us for properly dicharging
every duty. Fit us for death, and for heaven.
which we beg for Christ Sake. Amen.
Mercury this morning stands at 28°. The weather has
been open and fine for business up to the present period.
My stock of every kind looks quite as well or better than usual
I have provindes(?) of all kinds in abundance. My colts have
been running on the meadow without much feed, Sheep have
not yet been brought out of the fields & are fat. My Stock
of prork[sic] is Something over 4000lb will kill a beef shortly.
My stock on hand is 12 horses and colts, 18 head cattle
23 head of hogs, 16 head sheep. all in good condition
My family consists of self, wife, David William & John Henry
Bawzwill (sons) adn daughter Leonora Brown, & Niece
Mary Frances Wright, (6 Whites) Sarah & Abbey. her daugther,
Hetty, & Catherine 8, Maria 6, Joe 3, & Sam 3 months, (Hetty's children)
Jerry & Bob the last a hired man at $50 ; annum
in all 15 souls.
Attended at Mrs. Crouse, and hired out Jessee at
$50 to Dr. McClung & Edmond to Mr. Indy at $25-
and will keep Bob myself at $50-
1844 January 2nd Cloudy morning & like for rain
Mercury 32°. Evening, rain.
3rd Mercury 36°. Cloudy & foggy - (4th) My 32°. high wind
5th Mercury 26°. (6th) My 26°. (7th) Mercury 35 sermon
by Revd Morrison. Rented part of Tavern house for $36-
8th Mercury 30°. windy night & cold morning. sawing
posts & palings for Capt McChiniy (McChesney?). 9th My 26°. Snowing.
10th snow fell about 2 Inches deep, Mercury 32°. Collected $15
of Wallace on a/c of Robinson claim.
11th Mercury 22°. quite frosty. (12th) My 27°. cloudy.
13th My 45°. Mr. Davis & Mr. Keper with us last night. Evening
Miss Stuarts, Mr. Jas Walker, & Mr. Stuart, came home with Fanny.
SUnday 14th Mercury 32°. Cloudy morning sermon by Revd Morriosn.
Margaret Beard & Miss Virginia Gilman with us.
15th My 33°. sleeting. 16th My 33 still dark cloudy winter
17th Mercury 40° Still cloudy & raining. waters up fog continues.
Mr. Wm Kennedy buried to day after long confinement of 8 or 10 years
Miss Nancy Hutchinson buried yesterday who died suddenly.
attended singing school & had a large number of young
persons with Mr. Webster to sinug at my house. Evening
quite cold & windy. My 32°.
18th Mercury 30° very windy night company left at 10
19th My 28°. fair & Bright killed young beef 2 yrs old weighing 466 lb
hide 87 lb also 2 hogs 135 & 178 lb have killed 4096 lb pork
Pork & Beef 4562 lbs.
20th My 32 cold East wind. finished manuring my orchard
raw day & like for snow.
Sunday 21st Snowed 3 or 4 Inches last night cold morning
Mercury 26° Sermon by Revd Morrison. 22nd My 28°.
Tuesday 23rd Rain & snow last night, Foggy morning My 40°.
24th My 36°. Thrushing out oats cleaned up. Cold of oats 35 Bu[shels]
25th Fair, My 28°. (26th) My 12°. (27th) Mercury 6°. (28th) My 10°.
Monday 29th. My 10°. the last 4 days cold Mercury not
above 24° in that time. (30th) Still cold My 20°. Wednesday
31st Mercury 12° Threshed otu 15 bushels spring wheat
1844 February 1st Fair & frosty Mercury 14°. The weather
has been very cold for the last 8 days. Mercury not rising avove
the freesing point in that time. My corn fodder just fed out
have a good supply of hay, straw &@ [all] Stock in good order.
Friday 2nd Warm morning, Mercury 43°. rain & slett
yesterday. 3rd Mercury 36°. cloudy. will go for Lexington
snowed & sleeted abt 4 Inches. went to Mr. Beards.
Sunday 4th Mercury 27°. Still sleeting, returned home from Mr. Beards
Monday 5th Mercury 30°. Cloudy & somewhat foggy. Paid for
Lexington Gazette to Mr. Baldwin $2.50 up to Next August.
also Sent $2 to Saml D Patterson &@ [all] in advance to next Jany
(27th) when I ordered the paper to be stopped - money sent
on 3rd Jnst (handed to Patterson by Dr Gold)
Tuesday 6th still cloudy. Mercury 34°. I yesterday left $140
with A. Carson to be paid J. W. Culton on a/c Rogers.
7th Mercury 33°. (8th) Little snow last night, windy cold morning
Mercury 19°. little son J. Hy very unwell last night. clearning
off Cedar Hill. Threshed off clover seed.
Judgement apt Gregory & cash Wallce $7.75 (10th)
Friday 9th Mercury 18°. paid Mr. Webster 6/~ (10th) My 16°. Bright & clear
our little son John Henry still very unwell rests badly at night
Sunday 11th Fine frosty morning, Mercury 18°. Rested badly last night. John
slept but little & had high fevers, the effects of teething & probably
worms. has a bad cough & is very hoarse.
Monday 12th John Henry something bertter, Snow clouds, My 30°.
13th My 23°. Planked up East side of Barn. Song J.H. better.
14th My 34°. a Heifer calf from Hump. (the 8th)
15th My 34°. will send some Apples, Turnips, & potatoes to
Lexington by Jerry.
Friday 16th Mercury 36°. David with friend McCormick in company
with Doct Estill, Jordan, & Estile. send A. Crouse P note by
John Robinson to L.D. Davison ($75) paid James Randolph
$5 in advance for flax seed. Recd 5 Bushels
of flax seed from J. Compton. & cash for Apples &@ [all] $6.62
sent Colo Reid 3 bbls at 12/~ 1 Do to sloan $2-
1844 February 17th Mercury 36° Engaged Splitting wood & rails
The weather has not been favourable for out door business
for some weeks having been cold & variable ~
Sunday 18th Mercury 26th Fine clear morning. Sermon by Revd Morrison
19th My 26°. Splitting rails & wood. (20th) Mercury 36°.
Wedy 21st Mercury 38°. fine bright weather for some days.
22 fine day, Mercury 44°. Mrs. Jones will visit Brownsbg to day
after being housed up for abt 4 months.
Friday 23rd Mercury 34°. fine morning. Hawling out some manure.
24 My 40°. Cloudy & spitting snow, Paid Amy Peatross $15.
I am due her yet $15. When She will be paid infull for
the Pisgah land which I bought from her 5 years ago.
Sunday 25th Mercury 32°. Mrs Jones will go with me to church
to day, for the first time since last fall; little daughter
is now 2 months old. fine thrift child. Mr. Metcalf preached
for us to day
Monday 26th Mercury 31°. Still fine weather. Mr. Talley goes
for Lynchbujrg this morning, loaned him my roan mare.
27th Mercury 41°. (28th) Mercury 24°. cleaned out lime Kiln
Mr. Trimble with us all night ~ By cash of Billy Johnston $4-
Thursday 29th Mercury 32°. Fanny went to Kerrs Creek. Sowing
clove seed in chaff in field South from the house.
brought home 1 Load ground plaster.
March 1st. Fine morning, Mercury 40°. Ground getting
quite dry & forst generally out of the ground, & many
persons plowing.
2nd Mercury 57°. Ground 16 Bu[shels] flax seed & commenced
making oil.
Sunday 3rd Mercury 46°. Wheat fields begin to look green.
the fine weather for 2 weeks past has had a favorable
influence. The weather has been smokey & dark
for some days we now have a clear atmosphere
Monday 4th My 36°. will go to court Great Clay Meeting to day
1844 March 5th Mercury 22°. cold & clear, plowing
orchard by the house for spring wheat & oats.
6th Bright morning, My 27°. will go to Waynesborough to day
8th Returned from Waynesboro' in the rain, friends will.
Friday 9th Mercury 50°. cloudy with sprinkle of rain.
Sunday 10th Fine morning. Mercury 32°. Sermon by Revd
Morrison. (11th) Mercury 32°. (12th) Mercury 44°. cloudy
13th Merucy 52°. fine morning. (14th) My 44°. (15th) My 42° rain
16th Mercury 44°. Cloudy but mild weather for past week
17th A bright morning after a cloudy & wet week. My 42°
with high wind. Attended yesterday the funeral sermon of
Hugh. Hugh Stuart, a promising youth, who was cut down in
Early life. He died of Eresipelour. An excellent sermon preached
on the Occasion. by Revd Morrison.
Monday 18th My 34°. cold wind. Mrs. Brown & Mrs. Withrows
with us to day. Very windy. putting up line fence between
Mr. Beard & myself. (19th) Mercury 22°. Freezing weather. Repairing
finces, which are now in good order generally.
Jacob Palmer jr helped us to day & we put up abt
200 pannels & staked & ridered about the half of it -
Wednesday 20th Mercury 32°. (21st) Mercury 32°. Hawled in load
rails & stakes & made up fince between Mr. Trotter & Self,
part new rails (22nd) Mercury 24°. frosty. Got of Templeton Adair
&@ 14/4 Bushels flax seed for which I hpaid cash $10.69
Got also 7/~ Bushels seed from Mr. Brown & paid $4. this seed
worith 3/9 p Bushel. also 11 3/4 Bushels seed from Patteinson
worth 8.81¢. slight snow
Saturday (23rd) My 34°. spent day with Br. Samuel
Sunday 24th Mr. Calhoun preached for us to day. My 30°
Monday 25th Fine calm morning, Mercury 39°
will finish sowing orchard wist from the house
in Spring wheat & oats sowed 15 Bushels S.W. & oats.
26th My 46°. fine morning (27th) My 49°. children Go to
Waynesboro' to day.
1844 March 28th Mercury 34°. Plowing for oats
have sown abt 16 Bushels oats & S. Wheat to date
attended as one of the appraisers of Kennedy Estate.
Friday 29th Mercury 52°. fine growing weather. Has set out onions
winter Peas, & sown cabbages & but seed. went to Kennedys
sale, bought lot old barrels, still & old irons for 99 1/2 cents
& pair for same by clarking. Evening rain.
Saturday 30th Mercury 46°. Good rain & still cloudy waters upo
31st Frosty Mercury 28°. Sermon by Revd Morrison.
April 1st. Mercury 28°. fine clear morning. will go to Court
collected from Dr Graham $7/~ From Mr. Dunlap $12. &
paid James Compton $3.12/~ Infull for flax seed.
2nd Apl Fine morning. My 30°. Helped to raise house for
Enos Swink. 3rd My 33°. Paid Dr Badarack $4 for putting
teeth in order, also $32.44 to A. Patterson for P. Porter
Thursday 4th Mercury 50°. paid Dr. Badarack $2. For repairing teeth.
Sowed on field East from teh house on Beards line 17 Bushels of
oats & 1/~ Clover & Timothy seed.
5th My 50°. Took down school house. sowed flax seed
Saturday 6th Mercury 52°. Mr. Webster, Rise Beard & Miss McChesney
with us. Peach Trees & full bloom. fine weather.
Sunday 7th My 48°. Good sermon by Revd Morrison.
8th My 55°. Still fine weather. Mary F. Wright will
go to day to Lexington to school at Anne Smith
Academy. Evening, Brother Samuel Withrow died abt
4 Oclock very unexpectedly of Inflamation of the bowels
after being sick 4 days. He has left a helpless family
of 3 small children & wife. May God in his mercy
strengthen them to bear up under this afflection dispintion (?)
Tuesday 9th will attend Brother Samuels funeral to day
with family. Morning warm, My 62°. a calf each
from Margretta & Star
Wm. A. Beard with us.
1844 April 10th Fine morning, weather dry & windy Peach
trees in full bloom, also Peas & cherry trees out, & forrest
trees will be in leaf soon if not checked by cold weather. The
season may be said to be Early & some persons are planting
corn, I will not be ready for 10 days. My oats are up &
I am now just beginning to plow for corn.
Mercury 50°. Hawling down School House.
Thursday 11th Mercury 30°. (12th) My 55°. forrest trees out. Balm
Gilead has have as large as a dollar. (13th) My 54°. Spent
day at Brownsburg. Henry 13 J Withrow & Mary Gulley arrived there.
Sunday 14th Mercury 55°. Sermon by Revd AD Metcalf.
15th My 58°. will go to court. collected $46.08 of Crouse &
paid out to Brubeck for seed $[illegible]0- to Fanny ¢2-
Tuesday 16th My 63°. (17th) My 60°. fine rain (18th) still raining
Mercury 50°. Henry B.J. Withrow, Mary Withrow & Mary Gully
with us all night.
Friday 19th still raining with East wind for 2 days. My 40°. cold
unpleasant weather, Sacramental season commences to day.
20th Still cloudy, My 44°. sermon by Revd Wm Campbell.
Sunday 21st Mercury 48°. Foggy, growing morning. sermon by
Wm Campbell. (22nd) My 50°. (23rd) My 54°. (23rd) 60°.
Thursday 25th My 58°. will commence planting corn today
attended election & put up roof on S. House in evening.
26th My 55° (27th) My 59°. Lo adn S. Patterson my black
mare, Cala, to go to Winchester & further if necessary,
price put on her $60. Heavy rain in evening.
Sunday 28th Mercury 33°. Revd Morrison away at Presbytry.
29th Mercury 46°. finshed planting corn in field next Wards
have a lot of two yet to plant say abt 3 acres
Tuesday 30th My 42°. Gave Jacob Stoner $7 for Martin
Nevins to pay Note
1844 May 1st Mercury 30°. This may be said to
have been a unremarkable season, Spring opened a
month earlier than unusual. Everything looks green
& gay, & the prospect for an abundant harvest
has rarely been better.
Thursday 2nd My 65°. finished planting corn, planted Mangle Wurtzel
& melon seed (3rd) My 55°. planting some late potatoes
Saturday 4th My 64°. will go to Lexington to day with my
family, expect to be abset till Tuesday. Mr. Jacob Beard
died this morning abt noon.
Wednesday 8th Returned from Lexington & Mr. Beards
while absent paid J.D. Davidson 12$1/2 on a/c of
fees - also cahs for Hats, shoes, socks, &@ [all] $3~
Thursday 9th Mercury 46°. cool morning. clipping sheep
10th My 60°. (11th) My 60°. (Sunday 12th) My 72° sermon
by Revd Davies of N. Carolina.
Monday 13th My 44°. quite cool, wheat heading. & corn
ready to work. will go to Brownsburg to fix up
fences &@ [all]
Tuesday 14th Fine morning. My 58°. Making line fence on
south side & getting New groudn in order for potatoes
15th My 55° (16th) My 62° hands working on road, will go to
the Grove to day for flax seed for which I paid.
Sister Beard with us all night. a good shower.
Friday 17th My 68°. paid Patty Porter order to J. Miller $10 1/2
harrowing corn. 18th My 64°. Gent Muster. planting new
ground potatoes.
Sunday 19th Mercury 57°. opened Sunday School
to day. had a pretty good attendance. Sermons
by Revd Morrison & Davies. Collected $3 /~ for purchase
of Sunday School books. Hettys boy Sam died this Evening
of whooping cough.
1844 May 20th Mercury 58°. Growing morning.
Showry through the day. Finished plantingn late potatoes.
21st My 66°. Misting rain. (22nd) My 48°. cold East wind.
put in Whites Mill 40 flour barrels have there now 53.
Wednesday 23rd My 48°. working on chimney at school house
& replanting corn (24th) My 56°. (25th) My 61°. Still working at S. house
with 3 hands.
Sunday 26th My 66°. Sermon by Revd Morrison, a good attendance
at Sabbath school. rain in the evening, Seasonable weather.
27th My 64°. rain. (28th) My 60°. Still cloudy hazy weather.
29th My 62°. (30th) My 66°. (31st) Tornado passed over Brownsbg's Nuch my way down(?)
June 1st My 66°. Heavy rain this morning ground
too wet for plowing. 2nd My 50°. fine morning
Sunday 3rd Mercury 56°. fine morning. sermon by Revd Calhoun
Family all out to day. (4th) My 65°. borrowed of
Samuel Patterson 377 in plaster pd Mss P. Porter $4-
Wednesday 5th Mercury 58°. Cloudy wet weather (6th) My 58°.
Friday 7th My 64°. Hail & much rain to day. Family
in Brownbg. Hail distroyed some fields wheat & rye.
Saturday 8th My 62°. preparing to go to Richd with oil, Butter
& laird &@ [all]
Sunday 9th Mercury 67°. sermons by Revd Davis & Morrison
considerable rain in Evening.
Monday 10th My 64°. all tolerably well will go for
Richmond this morning.
Thursday 20th Returned from Richmond & found my
famiy in usual health for which I returend thanks
to God. The weather has been wet in the Velley
and contrary to expectiation there is much rested
wheat & the crop will hardly be an average
one in this neighhourhood. Oats looks well.
Sold my oil for $165.04 left 10 Gallons in Waynesboro forded
sold butter & lard for $15. 3/4 feather sofr $10. in all $190.78
purchased groceries to amt of $81.81 dry good hats &@ [all] abt $30
paid bill in Scottsville $15.40. chas in hand $77.
1844 Monday 22nd Fine morning, Mercury 60° had
comedarable(?) rain last night. Bad hay weather.
went to Mr. Beards Pale yesterday. purchashed wedge & rings 4/6
bu seap 1.18 cattle $20. Bed straw & Bedding.. moles & Canturn 3 Ga
Drawar 1.15 big wheel 3/~ in all $31.44/~ Due in 12 months.
will commence cutting rye to day. Mr. Paine boarding with us
Sunday 23rd Mercury 52°. cool morning bright & clear.
Waggon came home this morning.
Monday 24th My 55°. School commences to day. opened with
14 scholars. (25th) My 60°. cash for Lexington hawling
$12.64 (26th) My 61°. fine morning. (27th) My 68°.
will commence cutting wheat to day which has been
ready for several days.
Friday 28th My 71°. (29th) Mercury 62°. fine weather for a walk
Sunday 30th My 64°. cloudy & like for rain. cut wheat 2 1/2 days
Monday July 1st 1844
Fine morning, Mercury 70°. will go to court to day.
paid to Joseph W. Culton, on a/c of John Rogers
$112.45. also on a/c Nancy Porter $95.12 1/2 and
to Martha Porter in cash & groceries &@ [all] $193.78 in all
$471.35. Recd from Wm Taylor & D.d E. Moore $1279 12/100
Tuesday 2nd Mercury 70°. 3rd My 72°. cloudy with rain at noon
The weather has been very seasonable for weeks &
every thing grows finely. apples apricots & pears
ripe for a week past.
July 4th Fine morning, My 60°. c[l]ear & bright
finished cutting wheat - Some oats ready to cut
5th My 57°. James Mooney brought to Brownsbg
by Hy Withrow for stealing. Sam Sharp
6th My 75°. raining a little
Sunday 7th My 66°. Fine growing weather. Sermon
by Revd Morrison
1844 Monday July 8th, East wind, Mercury 66°.
Hawling in wheat. cutting oats & Hay. (9th) My 68°
Mr Morrison, Mrs Smith & Mrs Waklin & children spent
the day with us, Apricots gone.
Wednesday 10th will thrush wheat to day with Swoopes
Mashine. very warm, & getting dry, My 70°.
11th Mercury 66°. Cleared up 120 bushels flint wheat
threshed yesterday.
Friday 12th Mercury 64°. cleared up 63 bushels wheat to
day which with 58 sent to Mill, & 60 Bushels in work
Shop make altogether 185 Bushels. Threshed bushels
oats & Bushels rye to day. have yet to thresh abt
100 Bushels oats & spring wheat & abt 200 Bushels oats
Saturday 13th My 60°. Sold to Colo Brown of Albemarle
my mares Inde & cola for $65 & 60$ say $125
with Interest from teh datr, payable in 12 months
went to Church & heard an excellent sermon by
Revd Million also a good one from Mr. Skinner
Sunday 14th Mercury 64°. fine warm morning. Sermons to
day by Revd Skinner & Ben Smith. a Large congregation
out. 2 added to the church. Fine weather.
Monday 15th My 66°. Fanny will go to Waynesboro to day
16th My 71°. still cutting & putting up oats which
are a good crop. (17th) My 70°. fine harvest weather
18th Mercury 70°. (19th) My 66°. Talley working for himself.
20th My 72°. Hawling in Oats & cutting hay.
Sunday 21st. My 68°. Fair & getting quite dry. Sermon
by Revd Hy. Brown. 22nd My 71°. (23rd) My 72°.
24th My 70°. some rain last night. (25th) My 66°.
26th My 70°. some rain; 27th My 61°. East wind &
like for rain. Have 8 or 10 Tons hay down
cleared up 75 Bushels spring wheat, rye & oats to day
1844 July 28th Sunday, Mercury 61°. Sermon by
Revd Foot. gave $1. to Foreign Missions
Monday 29th Cool. Mercury 56°. Clear fine morning.
30th My 64°. rain bow, from S. to west. (31st) My 68°.
Thursday August 1st. Mercury 66°. 2nd My 66°.
visited friend McCormick & collected from hism $20
on a/c of odl Grove debts. a good rain.
Saturday 3rd Mercury 63°. sent to S. McCorcle $12 by John
Brooks. Present at Democratic Meeting at Fairfield which
numbered abt 35 members. rather a failure.
Sunday 4th My 70°. Sermon by Revd Jas & Hy Brown
5th My 60°. wen tot court. 6th My 64°. 7th My 59°.
8th My 58°. Sowing Turnip seed. cash Shephardson $7.
9th My 66°. making line fence with Waid. South.
Saturday 10th My 75°. very warm morning. (11th) My 72°
Sermony by Revd Morrison.
Monday 12th Mercury 53°. quite cool & dry. will sit out
for Louisburg this morning & expect to be gone
8 days.
Tuesday 20th Returned last Evening from Lewisburg.
had a pleasant trip & met with many distinguished
strangers. attended the sessions of the Sessions
of the Internal Improvement Convention. was
also at the hous of Doctor Hines, & Took back
the house & lot sold hime some years ago. for
the balance due on same -
The weather has been warm & dry & the corn
crop will be short.
Wednesday 21st Mercury 70°. Good rain last Evening &
still cloudy Mr. Taylor with us
22nd My 70°. Spent day at Stricklers Springs
23rd My 72°. Ditching in meadow for some days
Saturday 24th August 1844. Mercury 65°. dry weather.
finished ditching in meadow & plowing down banks &@ [all]
Sunday 25 My 55°. Mr. James Payne (of M) with us. sermons
by Revd James & Mr. Brown (26th) My 50°. 27th My 50° Mr.
R. & Miss Jame McNut & Mrs. E. Withrow spent the day with us.
28th Mercury 47°. quite cool - (29th) My 50° (30th) My 50°
Majr Brooks & family & Mrs Finley, Mr. Culton & Johnston to see us.
31sr My 64°. cloudy, Making peach butter. 18 Gallons from
50 Gallons cider & 3 bushels pealed peaches. should have been 4.
Sunday 1st Sept My 64°. Still cloudy without rain. very dry.
2nd My 63°. Fanny starts to day for school. commenced cutting
up small corn for fodder. (3rd) My 66°. (4th) My 55°.
7th My 60°. cool & windy. (6th) My 62°. (7th) My 54°. attended law
at Lusks. claimed attendance off Wright $1.08.
Sunday 8th My 60°. cloudy. sermon by Revd McFarland. (9th) My 56°.
10th My 54°. sold 2 Bbls flour to Mooney for $6 1/2 & 2 for $6. one to Swink
for 3/4 one to Paxton for 3 1/4 one to Mrs Smith for 3 3/4 in chickins
at bd 2 to Lotts for 6 1/2$ (11th My 56°.) pd Mr. J. Armstrong $2. Jos
Miller 3/~ (12th) My 50°. will go to court. paid McCorcle $2.
on a/c flax seed. collected $3.367 of Ro. white on a/c of
barrels.
14th Mercury 58°. Spent the day at Majr Brooks. Fanny
returned from Rice McNutts wedding. & set out again for
school.
15th Sunday. Mercury 56°. Sermon by Revd. A.D. Metcalf & Psalmody
explained by Revd. Morrison. (Monday 16th) My 58°. (17th My) 56°.
sent cash to Thomas Beard by Mr Beard $10. (18th) My 59°. (19th) 58°
20th My 61°. putting lap shingle roof on mill. Finished sowing
field in wheat next Wards. sowed 20 Bushels on the field
& orchard.
Saturday 21st. My 60°. a good shower of rain for an
hour. attended Walkers law, got judgement vd Balson for
$2.63 & Recd cost $6.
Sunday 22nd Mercury 50°. Have had bad cold for a
week, & very much pained in my Loins. (28th) Again down,
stairs, have been confined by stranguary & rhumatism for past 6 days
Saturday 28th Sept 1844 Haver had cloudy weather
for last 2 days with East wind & rain commenced last night
with the appearance of a good season after a long
continued drowth. which has been pretty general, the
crop of corn will be short, pastures are burnt out &
henbage of Every kind in a parched condition. The ground
has been so dry for many weeks as to be very difficult
to prepare for the wheat crop. We have now however the
appearance of a propitions season. and much may yet be
done for the fall crop. I have seeded to date about 30 bushels
of wheat in the orchard by the house near 3 bushels & in
the field next Mr. Waids abt 17 bushels & in corn field South
from the house 10 bushels, the ballance of the field is mostly
fallow land which I am now plowing & hope to get seeded
next week. An this price of land I will sow 10 bushels
making in all sown 40 bushels. with some patches on
which I will so abt 5 bushels.
Sunday 29th My 40° windy night, & cool morning. The rain
has been quite a good one & the ground is now wet
Mrs. Jones & Willie went to church, I am able to to sit up
nearly all day. Very rheumatick in my left leg
Monday 30th My 44°. Bright fine morning. Making stone
fence at he mill.
Oct 1st Mercury 41°. This day I am 47 years old.
2nd Mercury 44°. fine morning. 3rd My 52° Killed a
small heifer weighing 353lb neat price for meat hide &
tallow $14.38 cost me $6 last spring. Frds Trimble & Love with us.
Friday 4th My 46°. fine shower last night, sowed lot next
garden in Good Wheat. one bushel sown, also 1/2
bushel sown on Turnip patch of Mediteranian wheat
Saturday 5th My 46°. finished sowing field South
from teh house sowed 19 bushels, 10 some
time ago & 9 to day. Have sowed up to date
41 Bushels & will sow abt 4 more which
will complete my fall sowing. Recd cash of
John Nelson $2. for oil, loaned same to J. Qlair.
1844 Oct 25th Mercury 54°. Mr. Withrow will be
buried to day at noon.
Saturday 26th My 52°. fine morning. Husking & putting up
corn. Have put away my potatoes which are a
small crop. say120 to 130 Bushels.
Sunday 27th Fine warm morning. Mercury 58°. sermon by
Revd Paxton. Fine rain in Evening. Gent Dorman with us
Monday 28th my 50°. waters quite flush this morning & still raining
29th My 36°. Recd cash of Mucp for Bason $16 Due him
for hawling Bacon &@ [all] $1.77
Wenesday 30th Mercury 32° Cold & windy for last 2 days. Left $30
with Miss E. Wade to be sent to Brubeck & Armstrong. I am
yet due them $18 on load of 64 Bushels of flax seed.
Thurday 31st. My 32°. Fair fine morning, will for Lexington to day to
attend the fair. Nov. 2nd My 40° Killed Beef for Mr. Davis
weighting 585 lb (3 years old. ) Fine day. Hawling in corn
in the stocks
Sunday 3rd Mercury 40° Sermon by Revd Morrison (4th) My 45°.
attended Election of President & Vice President to day
at Brownsburg, Clay & Frelinghuysen, Whigs, Polk & Dallas, D.
H 1840 V.B. Brownsburg Precinct 192 Whig 109 Democrats
Whig 638 548
638 Whig 555 Democratic (535) 697 (149 Whig Majority)
535 Whig Majority 103 548 103 46 gain on 1840
Paid Sherriff clerks Tickets $24.29 Paid A. M Masters $25
Recd from Echin $2
Tuesday 5th Mercury 42°. (6th) My 34°. (7th) My 38°. 8th My 48°.
9th My 40°. (10th) My 45°. very fine weather. sermon by
Revd Calhoun. (11th) My 50°. (12th) My 57°. Killed 2 Hogs
weighing 190 & 200 lbs 390 lb (13th) My 54°. 14th My 32°.
15th Mercury 29° sacramental season.
Saturday Nov 16th 1844 Mercury 34°. Sermon by
Revd McFarland
Sunday 17th My 44°. pleasant wetaher. sermon by Revd
McFarland. a large congregation & fine day. (18th) 48°.
moderate rain The season has been remarkably fine for 2
months, and small grain looks well.
Thursday 19th Mercury 26°. frosty morning. (20th) My 36°. rainy night.
21st Foggy morning, My 44°. (22nd) My 46°. rainy. took up
Beef to Mr. Davis weighing 664 lb brought home 228 lb Iron.
23rd Mercury 46°. fine morning after hard rain in the night.
Sunday 24th Windy night, Mercury 35°. Mr. Morrison abest at Bethel.
25th cold morning, after 2 days high wind. Mercury 20°. fair hard
Doct Gold $10. Infull for medical services. (26th) My 24th.
27th My 50°. fine day, Killed 2 beeves 462 & 680 lbs part
for Mr Davis say 982 lb. (28th) My 36°. Rainy morning, will
go to Forge to day for iron & flax seed. RecD R. B Anderson
4 3/4 Bushels flax seed paid cash $3.56 of Randolph 13 3/4 pd
cash infull $10.31. (Friday 29th) Mercury 46°. Fine morning.
Saturday 30th My 44°. cloudy. waggon loaded with 10 Bbl, flour
& 25 Gallon oil for Scottsville. By cash Mr. Withrow $108.
Sunday 1st December Cloudy morning, My 45°. Monday 2nd
Mercury 42°. still cloudy. started waggon to Scottsville, gave
Jerry cash $2.50
Tuesday 3rd My 32°. Cold East wind. Sold Majr Brooks 13 head
cattle for $100 - 7 Calves, 3 Earlings, & 3 steers. Friends
James & Mr Trimble with us. Sold the old gentleman
a load of Iron at $100 p Ton
4th My 36°. fine day (5th) My 41°. (6th) My 44°. (7th)
Mercury 36°. raining & windy. wrote to Geo. Davis to forward
receipt &@ [all]
Sunday 8th Mercury 34°. windy night & still blowing. Sermon
by Revd Morrison (9th) Mercury 25°. will kill hogs
to day (12 Killed) weighing abt 2000 lbs Jerry
returned from Scottsville (10th) My 22°. Fair & frosty.
1844 Wednesday 11th December. Frosty morning Mercury 24°
have salted and dry abt 2300 nice port & have 6 Hogs
yet to kill which will weight 7 to 800 lb paid J. W.
Culton $2 infull for flax seed. Hogs weighed (1013 pound)
Thursday 12th Merucry 20°. (13th My 38°. (14th) My 34° went to Forge
& got 475 lb Iron from Mr. Davis for which I paid cash $15.13
Ham murmans fee 3/~ (15th) Mercury 31°. sermon by Revd N. Sr
Monday 16th My 24°. Jerry started to Scottsville with 14 Bbls flour
gave him cash $3. 2 Inches of snow. cold wind, (17th) My 20°
(18th) still cold, My 18°. (19th) My 28°. cloudy (20th) My 33°. Mr. Thompson
get 34 Gallons oil & brought 32/4 flax seed pd cash 9/~ recd cash
of Hanger 6/~ (yesterday)
Saturday 21st Mercury 24°. fine morning. Jerry returned from Scottsville
Mare died in Scottsville worth abt $70 -
Sunday 22nd Mercury 30°f foggy morning. sermon by Revd Morrison
23rd Mercury 30°. slight snow, windy unpleasant morning
24 Fine cold morning, Mercury 26°.
Wednesday 25th Mercury 28°. fine weather & a quiet Christmas
26th My 42°. Sent load iron to Mr Trimble Recd cash of
Ellio 9/~ through Mr Withrow. (27th) Mercury 46°. raining.
28th My 24°. clear fine morning.
Sunday 29th My 28°. Bright frosty morning. sermon by by Revd
Morrison, who was taken sick in church, but soon got better
30th My 44°. 31st My 45°. Paid J.W. Payne $9.12/~ for tution
January 1st. Mercury 51°. Remarkably fine weather, for
the season. We would unite in returning thanks to our
God for the many mercies, & favours confered on us
during the peast year, and would pray God to
still continue his goodness unto us. To bear
with our imperfections, & to Enable us to discharge
all our relative duties a right in his sight.
Purchased of Doct Js. McClung, his boy Cyrus, for
whom I paid $210. Cyrus is between 8 & 9 years old
& a sprightly boy.
1845 January 2nd Mercury 34°. FIne day 3 Mrs Withrowh
to see us with lots of children. Jerry set out for Scottsville
with 14 Bbls flour pd Alexander $4 1/2 infull.
Friday 3rd My 36°. (4th) Mercury 40°. very windy night sold
my pisgah land to Henry Lucas & son for $200. to bear Jd
from 11th March 1845. went to Fairfield as witness. Mard
vs McKinsey. Collected $10. fine each, from Killy (Kitty?) & A
Troxill. also $300. from D. Brown
Sunday 5th Mercury 43°pleasant morning (6th) My 46°. rain & snow &
sleet & hight wind all day. Sent $50 cash to Doct McClung by
James Withrow. (7th) My 36°. grouind covered with sleet. Mr. Galley
to see us (8th) My 36°. (9th) My 34°. clear frosty morning. Paid
Mrs Grouse $20 paid Doct. McClung infull for the
purchase of his Boy Cyrus supposed to be 8 years old.
also paid Bill for services on Jipee $30. paid to
Mr. McGuffin yesterday $15 for flax seed. 10th My
43°. killed 6 Hogs weighting 1013 in all 3313 pounds.
Saturday 11th Mercury 30°. Heigt of snow last night (Mr. Gulley up)
collected $6.50 of weight, $9.15 assumed by P Trotter to be
paid in 2 weeks. Int from 1st Jany 1845 title paid
Sunday 12th Mercury 28°. John Henry & Leonora been quite unwell
with bad colds & Teething for last 10 days. Sermon by Revd Morrison
from Revolation 19th & 16th.
Monday 13th Mercury 30°. clear & frosty. (14th) My 29°. clear.
15th Mercury 31st. (16th) My 42°. (17th) Mercury 52°. raining
18th My 46°. fine rain. paid John McBride $6 infull
for flax seed
Sunday 19th Mercury 24°. Hazy & like for snow. Sermon
by Revd Morrison. snow & sleep in Evening (20th) My 29°.
Tuesday 21st My 44° in Browsnburg fixnig up stable 22nd My 34°
Thursday 234d My 28°. still fixing stable in Brownsburg. put up logs
24th My 38°. East wind & much rain. (25th) My 40°.
Sunday 26th My 34°. fine bright morning. excellent sermon by Rd Payne
29th My 30°. 28th My 34°. Hetty confined with twins, a boy & Girl.
29th My 34° one of the twins died, will go with family for Lexington.
1845 February 1st Returned from Lexington
after an absence of 4 days with my family
spent 2 nights, with Mr. Withrow, whose my
niece Mary Frances Wright has ben boarding
for the last 5 months. Had a very agreeable
trip. came round by Mr. Beards, where we
spent an agreeable night. The last 3 days
has been cold bracng weather, My at 25°.
Sunday 2nd Mercury down to 14°. coldest morning this winter.
Sermon by Revd Morrison. (3rd) My 16°. (4th) My 28°. snowed
last night about 4 Inches (5th) Stormy weather, Mercury 18°.
Hettys Baby, died last night being 8 days old (6th) My 17°. still
very story, high winds for 3 days
Friday 7th Mercury 15°. still cold morning. Hawling hay. (8th) My 28°
Sunday 9th My 24°. Long sermon by Revd Morrison.
10th My 24°. fine frosty morning. (11th) My 46°. quite pleasant
weather, Mrs. Mr & James Withrow, Patterson Brooks &@ to drive.
Wednesday 12th Mercury 58°. went to Kerrs Creek & Lexington. paid
Andrw Withrow $30 for board of Mary Fr Write for last
5 months. (13th) My 40° Mrs Wilion & Friend Trimble to
dinner with us.
Friday 14th cloudy morning, My 30°. (Evening good rain 15th)
Sunday 16th My 36°. an excellent sermon by Revd Morrison.
17th My 32°. 18th My 36°. (19th) My 36°. Spent Day yesterday
at Patsy Porters Trying with others to setlle ditching a/c
between her & Dennes Igo. Mrs Talley had a song last night
Thursday 20th My 44°. fine warm days, plowing for corn
21st Coz John Edgar with us. My 54°. 22nd My 56°.
Sunday 23rd South wind, & warm weather for 4 days. My 60°.
sermon by Revd Morrison. rainy day.
Monday 24th My 40°. Buds much swilled and every
appearance of an Early spring. ash Tree in bloom.
25th My 33°. (26th) My 44°. Digging fish pond. 27th My 28°
paid Martha Porter $50. Remitted G. Davis $300. 28th My 32°.
1845 March 1st Fine morning, My 36°. Mr. Devine
& Mr. McGill have been engaged 8 days in digging out
a fish pond for me at 3/~ p Day $4 - Attended at Fairfield
to day in behalf of Miss P. Porter, and got case Igo vs
Porter dismissed at Igos cost, als claimed attendance in
case Ward vs McKinnie, clained attendance 2 days $1.06.
Have plowed my oats ground & ready to sow, also some
5 acres corn land. paid crouse $98.03 Infull to 1-Nov 44
Mr. King made 1 pr coarse shoes, & 3 pr force shoes, & done mending
3/4 of a day.
Sunday 2nd Fine morning, My 46°. excellent sermon by
Revd Morrison. 3rd My 59 will go to court to day.
4th My 40°. President Polk inaugerated to day. cloudy & like for
rain. (5th0 My 40°. still cloudy. Finished fish pond and
paid Devinie & McGill $7 in full for Their services in help'g
to dig it, being abt one half the cost.
Thursday 6th Mercury 32°. (7th) My 43°. Fine weather apricot in bloom
rcd from Mrs. Gables $3 1/4 for 1 bbl flour. Cleaned up 3
bushels clover seed.
Saturday 8th My 52°. Charming Spring weather. planted Early potatoes
onions, beet seed, lettice, radish & sowed cabbage seed
Sunday 9th My 63°. sermon by Revd Morrison (10th) My 42°. rain
11th My 38°. Fair & windy, after a good rain () 12th My 29°.
Thursday 13th Mercury 35°. sowed 2/~ Bushels clover seed in fields next Wards
Friday 14 My 40 fine rain last night, enclosed remaining halve
of $300 to Geo. Davis of Penna to be mailed tomorrow. paid
Brubeck & Armstrong $20 on a/c flax seed. Dr. W J Armstrong $5-
Saturday 15th My 34°. windy. unpleasant day. (Sunday 16th, My 32°.
heard sermon by Mr. Payne of Fairfield. (17th) My 44°. went to
Forge and got 300 lb Iron from Kelly on a/c Mr Withrow jr &@
& 125 lb for self on a/c 50 lb Bacon. all left at Chambers
shop, 13 pieces. 18th My 35°. (19th) My 23°. ground frozen.
Monday 24th My 40°. I have been confined to may room for last 5
days by sickness. The weather during that time has been cold & windy,
Mercury hanging from 18°, to 27°. early bloom killed.
1845 March 24th The weather has been cold & windy and the
Earth frozed for near a week. The ground is now dry
and looks favourable for business I hope to be able
to get out to day for a little season. I have been
much afflicted with cold, pains in my limbs & bowels.
Tuesday 25th Mercury 34° Sowing oats (26th) My 29°. frosty Nv. trillsons (?)
school will commence to day. Emma & Carry with us.
27th Mercury 40°. (28th) My 40 finished sowing oats & clover seed
Sowed 2 Bushel of the latter, & 21 of the former on field N.E
Saturday 29th My 44° Sowing paster & ashes on clover &@ [all]
30th My 45° fine morning sermon by Revd Ruffner.
Monday 31st My 55° brought home from McDoway 13 Bu[shels] flax seed &
paid infull for the same. Spent Evening Mr. Willsons
Tuesday 1st April My 58°. will go for seed to New Port. pd $11 1/4
infull for seed. in all $61.25 at that place
Wednesday 2nd My 42°. 3d My 44°. very dry weather for near
a month. (4th) My 60°. windy & dry Bought George Ward 20
acres of land adjourning the land formally purchased
from him at $12 p acre paid when I am to get
papepion & hay the ballance $126.80 The strip of land I am to
get, is to be 40 rods wide & abt 80 pols long & Wade to make the fences
Saturday 5th My 55°. (Sunday 6th) My 44°. very smoky weather
for a week past & much fire in the mountains
which has done considerable damage in burning fence
& some good dwellings. Sermon by Revd Calhoun
Monday 7th My 36°. Miss Mary Potter with us to weave, windy & dusty
8th My 28°. cold & windy. (9th) Merecury down to 22°. I fear
the peaches are all killed. also most of apples
Thursday 10th My 42°. 11th My 48°. (12th) My 34°. frosty & clear
Sunday 13th My 44°. Still fair & very dry sermon by
Revd Morrison. (14th) My 59°. will go to court. paid
Gent Dorman $300. paid D.E. Moore $10. J.D. Davidson $9.50
April 15th 1845 Fine morning with Sprinkle of rain
Mercury 56°. (16th) Mercury 48°. planting corn. $10
paid A. Patterson for 50 bushels oats to be delievered by
Mr. Reid. also paid him $2. to have Stirrups plated
Thursday 17th My 56°. (18th) My 54°. Sent Jerry to Lexington cont. (?)
oil & Potatoes. put up Spring house. finished planting corn
lots. (19th) Mercury 52°. 20th My 50°. Some little yarn friday night.
sermon by Revd Morrison (Monday 21st My 42°. clear & bright
Tuesday 22nd My 40°. still clear & dry. 23rd My 50°. making rail,
& getting tan bark (24th) My 60°. Mr. King put up a cooking
stove till I can get mine repaired. (25th) My 64°. very warm
Saturday 26th My 50°. finished cutting down new ground South from
the house & will hawl hay to day. Hawled 3 good loads sy 4 Tones
27th My 60°. sermoney by Revd Morrison. Mr. Curry dined with us.
Monday 28th My 59°. (29th) Mercury 62°. Still very warm, My at noon 86.
Wednesday 30th My 62°. Showry weather. paid Mr. Carson $1.00 to
be sent in advance for the Star.
Thursday 1st May. Mercury 59°. growing weather. Presbytry
in Session at Lexingon. (2nd) My 61°. 3rd My 45°. settled
court & paid Mary Porter $3.58 for weaving 37 yds Tow
cloth at 3d & 24/! yards Linen Janes at 6d.
Sunday 4th Mercury 64°. Cloudy & like for showers, rain
much needed on Sugar Creek, have not had a good
one for 2 months. Sermon by Revd B. SMith, some rain
Monday 5th My 62°. Cloudy. good rain. (6th) My 53°. cloudy
(Miss Kerr married)
Wednesday 7th My 50°. good rain yesterday & now seasonable
8th cool morning My 40°. (9th) Mercury 42°.
10th My 52°. Gent Muster to day.
Sunday 11th My 54°. sermon by Revd Wm Beard & Ben Smith
12th My 55° Finished planting new ground corn.
13th My 60° replanting corn (14th) My 58°. will plant
potatoes. (15th) My 60°. some rain (16th) My 40°.
1845 May 17th Mercury 44°. Sacramental season.
Miss Campbell & Beard with us. pleasant weather.
sermons again by Revd Campbell & Beard.
Sunday 18th Mercury 50°. Fine morning. sermon by Revd
Campbell & Morrison. (19th) My 57v. (20th) My 60°.
21st My 55°. Seasonable weather. waggon at Waynesboro'
for seed, took down oil 36/~ Gals & Iron by Mr. Talley
2nd Fine morning Mercury 55°. building fence
through the woods to Wellions line. paid to
James Walker $253.33 part of which I recd
from Mr. Withrow pay $228.76
Friday 23rd Mercury 60°. Shower last Evening, 24th My 49°.
Waggon returned from Waynesboro with seed 43 1/4 Bu[shel] &
sundry goods. 25th Mercury 40°. quite cool & clear, Sermons
by Revd Morrison & Beard (26th) cool morning My 40°. Mingo sterd
Tuesday 27th My 44°. Mrs Jones abest at Brother Johns baking cakes.
28th My 54°. (29th) My 60°. Brother John Withrow to be married
this Evening. returned from wedding abt 8 PM.
30th will dine at Brother Johns with wedding party
Mercury 39°. clear & cool. Large company dined at
Br. Johns day 80 to 90 persons.
Saturday 31st May calm cool morning. Mercury 38°.
Sunday June 1st My 44°. attended preaching at Mount
Carmel by Revd Payne. Sister Withrow from Lexington
spent night with us
Monday 2nd Juen My 50°. will go to court accompanied
by Revd McNut & sisters. Callected $18.37 from Willson & @.
3rd My 52°. will go to Waynesboro to day.
7th Returned from Waynesboro, with supply goods. also
collected $30 from Wm Withrow on a/c of rent & of E. A. Wayland
$65 cash & one saddle $20. due by Mr. Wayland abt $40.00
sent James Walker $40 p Mr. Trotter & settled a/c with Wm Withrow
Saturday June 7th 1845 My 65°. dry weather grass short
corn & grass Short & pasture fields getting quite short.
Sunday 8th warm morning My 65°. in heat of day 90° to 94°
sermon by Revd Morrison.
Monday 9th My 70°. will cut clover for hay. which is a
very light crop. 10th My 66°. cloudy. (11th) My 75°. Hot day
12th My 66°. still very dry. sent 21lb veal to J. & Ja Kelly & 21lb Mr. Wright $2.10
had a fine rain of an hour, planted out cabbage, beet, & tomatoe
plants. also set out sweet potatoe slips. planted Irish potatoes.
Friday 13th Mercury 64°. growing morning. (14th) Mercury 68°. put
up 2 Loads clover hay. crop very light.
Sunday 15th Mercury 54°. cool morning. clear fine growing weather.
Sermon by Revd Morrison (16th) My 68°. (17th) My 60°. quite unwell
18th cloudy My 57°. something better. (19th) My 66 harvest Early this
season, many persons cutting for a week. I will commence
to-morrow. planted some sweet potatoe slips. good shower
Foggy morning 20th My 64°. rain & quite seasonable 21st My 66°
sowed 2 Bu[shels] buck wheat
Sunday 22nd Mercury 66°. rainy morning. continued to rain
all day. Now very seasonable. (23rd) My 72°. cutting wheat.
24th My 67°. Mr King with us. (25th) My 68°. fine weather.
Bought cooking stove at $65- paid in old stove & Balance
Thursday 26th My 58°. paid Mr. Willson $6 Tuition fees for
S.E. Gulley & David William. 27th My 60° fine harvest weather
wheat good but splightly rusted.
28th Cloudy, Mercury 64° will finish cutting wheat to day.
Sunday 29th My 60°. Sermon by Revd Morrison pleasant
day & fine congregatoin with some 70 Sabbath School
scholars
30th Mercury 60°. will go to cout & try to sell some colts
Boys hawling in grain & Plowing for buch wheat
There were few perosns at court. sold no
colts -
1845 July 1st Fine cool morning, Mercury 53°.
Still plwoing for buck wheat, first sowing up
2nd Still pleasant weather My 55°. will finish sowing
buck wheat.
Thursday 3rd Mercury 67°. cloudy & like for rain, a shower
4th Mercury 51°. fine bright day. 5th clear & cool My 50°.
Spent the day at Squire McNutts, with a pleasant party
Sunday 6th Mercury 60°. Sermons by Revd Beard & Morrison &
a good and prompt attendance at Sabbath School
7th Mercury 68° Spent day at Revd Morrisons
Tuesday 8th My 68°. (9th) My 72°. The mercury has ranged above
90° at heart of the day, for some days, ground very dry.
and water failing in many places. May God in his
mercy viist us with a gracious rain.
Thursday 10th Mercury 70°. hot dry weather. Dr. Grant pulled a front
Tooth for Willie. 11th My 62°. clear as a Bell (12th) My 64°
Sunday 13th My 65°. Sermon by Revd Morrison. 4 P.M. My 94°
14th My 70° (15th) My 68°. 16th My 70°. very hot weather
for a week past My ranging in heat of day to 94°
Thursday 17th My 74°. Light showers. putting up hay & harvesting oats
commenced threshing wheat.
Friday 18th My 72°. Threshed in one day 125 Bushels clean wheat
5 Bushels not so clean. & 10 Bushels screenings. put in
garner for seed 100 Bushels. & in hogs head 28 bushels
beaded wheat. Goose 11- Mediteranian 14- screenings, say 3.
Saturday 19th My 66°. Still threshing . a good shower.
20th Mercury 68°. Foggy morning. sermon by Rd Morrison
Monday 21st My 70°. Threshed out load oats & had 41 Bushels
22nd My 75°. Still very hot wehater. 23rd My 64°.
Sent to Whites Mill 2 loads wheat 125 Bushels & will
tomorrow send 75 Bushels more have put away for
seed &@ [all] 130 bushels paid Swoope toll 15/~ Bu[shel] & yet to
