thresh abt 15 Bushels - 360 Bushels in all.
Thursday 24th My 52°. cool, Fair, & dry will go to springs today
to repair cabbin
1845 July 25th My °59 Sacramental season commenced
Sermon by Revd Wm Brown. (26th) Mercury 64°. sermon by
Revd Hy & Wm Brown finished cutting meadow, very light crop of
grass.
Sunday 27th Merucry 64°. Sermons by Rev Wm & Hy Brown day fine &
dry. Monday 28th My 56°. 29th went to Springs at Stricklers
with family. Thursday 31st My 60°. had good shower of
rain yesterday. plowing cow pen for Turnips. which
I will sow to day.
August
Saturday 1st Got home from Stricklers Springs after an
absence of near 3 weeks; spent the time agreeably. The
weather has been pleasant with an occasional rain
& the ground is now in good order for plowing fallows
have plowed abt 25 acres of wheat stubble & will commence
fallow land to ady. pastures are very short and the
drowth has been severe. Crops of corn will be short.
Sunday 17th Mercury 68°. fine growing morning. Seasonable
wheather for a week past and ground in fine order
for plowing.
Mondnay 18th My 67°. Cloudy & raining a little (19th) My 69°. Still cloudy.
20th My 68°. 21st. My 66°. Hawling out manure for last 2 days
on wheat land. 22nd My 66°. 3 P My My 98°. Evening, rain.
Sunday 23rd Fair, My 68°. Sermons by Revd Morrison.
Jacob Supinger, moved in my house at 2$ p month rent
Monday 24th Fine growing morning. My 64°. Still hawling
out manure. (26th) My 68°. Delightful morning. (27th) My 70°.
fine rain in Evening. finished hawling out manure.
28th My 66°. 29th Cloudy * cool My 62°. (30th) My 62°. still cloudy
Sunday 31st Mercury 70°. fine morning & growing weather.
sermons by Revd Morrison, Dimissed Sabbath
Sc[h]ool for the season.
1845 September 1st Clear fine morning, Mercury 69°. I will
go to court to day. The boys will commence seeding
next Mr Waids, have in soak 5 Bushels Goose wheat in
brine to be roled in lime. 2nd returned from court
McKinsey sent on for further trial & goes to Goal.
3rd warm Morning, mercury 75°. finished sowing wheat in
field next Mr. Waids 8 bushels Goose & 2 of Mediteranean
wheat sown. last year sowed 17 Bushels on same field
which produced a good crop of heavy wheat 65lb p bushel
have sown to date 14 1/2 Bushels wheat 6/~ being Mediteranean
Thursday 4th My 72°. Cloudy warm weather. My aup to 90° yesterday
5th My 68°. getting dry, weather still hot. have sowed to date
20 and a half bushels wheat, 12/~ being Medeteranean, mostly
sown in field South from the house. All put in
well.
Saturday 6th My 59°. 3 bushels white wheat sown to date 11/2 in
field South west from the house & up in new ground field
being 23 bushels Sown to date
Sunday 7th My 57°. sermon by Revd Morrison.
8th My 68° a good shower at noon (9th) My 64°. raining
19th fine day finished seeding in field S. from the
house sowed 6 Bushels white wheat on same
Thursday 11th My 49° fine day. visited Revd Payne.
commenced cutting tops of corn have
been feeding fattining hots since 8th
sent miss Brooks & Wade a quarter of veal
Easch weighitn abt 90 lb Mr. King Mended some
shoes for which I paid him in bacon.
Friday 12th My 58°. will go to court to day James Mooney
Tried & sent to Penitentiary for 3 years
13th My 60°. cash of J.M. Willion $19. 1/4 Bought 3 bushels
clover seed of Majr Brooks at $5~ pd cash.
Mrs. Beard with us.
Sunday 14th Sept 1845 rainy morning. Mercury 62°.
sermon by Revd Morrison. 15th My 62°. 16th at court as
witness vs McKinsey. Bought 10 Bakewell sheep of Dr.
Leyburn. also 1 fine Devon & Durham Bull calf. Paid
for same in order from F. Payne on Dr. L. Have
now with Dr. Leyburn 10 ewe Lambs 1 Buck, a present, &
1 fine Bull calf say 6 weeks old.
Wednesday 17th My 55°. cutting up corn. 18th My 54°.
19th My 60°. putting away fodder. 20th plowing corn Land My 59°
Sunday 21st Mercury 62°. good rain last night. Sermon by Revd Mor[riso]n
Monday 22nd My 46°. will attend to laying off Down ry let (?)
for Mrs. Robt Alexander. (23rd) Some frost Mercury 41°.
sowed 1/2 Bushels Spelt. Traded cords with Mr. James Willsion
gave $4. bood bought calf at $2. & sold sow & 8 pigs for $8
au me by W. Willion $2 in grain. Loaned Geo Ward $2.
24th sowing wheat on corn lot next work shop. 2 bushels of
white wheat & 5 bushels flint. ground turned over with
Livingston plow, & sowed without harrowing. My 48°.
went to Furance wheat sown to date 35 Bushels.
Thursday 25th My 40°. will go to Mr. McFadons sale to day, bought
lot od irons of 1.80 cash, sold James McNut filly Julia at
$45.25 Ott & Dove colt at $50. Arthur McMasters $9 - for cow
And w Wipple cow for $9.25 Jos W Culton 5 calves for $10.02 1/2
Inall $123.52 1/2 Traded mar[e]s with Jack Beard and
gave boot in cash $10 - got filly Bill 3 years old
26th My 40°. waggon start this morning for Ric.d
with 112 Gallons oil, 2 firkins butter, 12 Bbls flour
Mr. Lowman & Jerry drive (27th) 48°.
Sunday 25th My 54°. Mr. Armstrong preached for
us to day.
Monday 29th My 50°. fine morning will go for
Recd. to day.
1845 Oct 7th Returned from Richd after an absense of 10
days. had a pleasant trip Sold my flour for $4.75 & oil
at 75 cents butter 14 & 17th cents. all bay filly $55. admounting
in the whole to $211.19 Bought Sunday bills goods &@ [all]
amounting to $108.06 expenses to & from Richd $5.62
8th My 62°. Heavy washing rain last night 9th My 64°
will go to Grove with sugar & salg to day. bought home
13 1/4 seed from Randolph & 14 1/4 from Adams paid for
some in Lawling of 75 p hhd & salt at $3 1/2 p sack
10th My 62°. raining for last 24 hours. ground very wet & waters
much refreshed after a long drouth. paid Patsy & Sally Porter $100.
There has been much rain Since Wednesday night & the
dry Easrth is now saturated with water.
Sunday 12th Mercury 50° prospect of clear weather. No
preaching to day Mr. Morrison abest at Synod Charlottesville
Monday 13th Frosty morning. My 37°. 14th My 40°.
15th My 46°. Seeding new ground.
Thursday 16th Mercury 31°. some ice. fine weather for some days.
Mr. Talley left the mill to day (17th) My 32°. 18th My 40°
finished seeding sowed on corn land in new ground
7 1/2 Bushels. Have sown 42 1/2 In all. The last not
rolled in lime. Digging potatpes which are but
a moderate crop.
Sunday 19th Mercury 40°. fine weather. No sermon to day
Revd Morrison sick. Prayer meeting by Revd H Walker
20th My 48°. (21st) My 44° Digging potatoes which are
tolerably good. 22nd My 29° Still on potatoes
23rd My 27°. Mr. Talley moved to day. to Dr. McClungs place
24th Mercury 30°. Sacramental Season commenced
to day. Sermon by Revd H Farland
25th My 36°. sermon by Revd Brown & McFarland.
Sunday 26th merucry 36°. Revd Morrison still quite ill
meeting conducted by Revd McFarland Brown & Paxton
27th Recd cash from James Withrow for waggon sold by
Hardin of Richd $80.75 - Got of Rd Gordon Thirty
seven & a half bushels corn on a/c of Mare sold
him last Spring - at $23 - corn at 40 cents say $14.20
yet due $8.80
Tuesday 28th My 40°. fine weather for past 10 days.
engaged hawling in corn. 29th still engaged at corn
My 40°. netted 16 partridges. 30th My 40°. still fine weather
Albert Miller moves to day. to have the house at a
rent of $18 - p anum. & to be pd for labour at teh
rate of $10 p month hr finding himself.
Sold James Withrow my cow Start for $12. cash.
Fiday 31st Mercury 42°. finished digging potatoes crop 140 B
Nove 1st Fine morning, My 55°. Evening fine rain.
Sunday 2nd Mercury 56°. went night & morning. Run quite full, &
still raining. Service by Revd Paxton. wet day till 2 P.M.
Mnoday 3rd My 42°. fine morning after a good rain.
4th My 40°. cloudy. Skift of snow at night. (5th) My 39°
6th My 46° will go to Kerrs Creek to day. Returned on 8th had
a pleasant trip. was at Lexington paid Professor Armstrongs
Tickets $3 - Also paid A. Withrow $8.80 for a wardrobe
purchased by him for me of C.W. Wayne.
school commnenced 19th By Mr. S. Humphreys
Sunday 9th My 34°. Windy cool morning. Sermon by
Revd Ben Smith, Blustering cold day. 10th My 36° will
kill some hogs to day. Killed 11 small hogs weighing
1548 average 141 lb nearly. (11th) My 38°. fine weather.
10th fine day. sister Mary & Caroline & mrs Susan
Withrow spent day with us. Sister mary very
unwell. 12th Sister Mary still quite unwell
sent for Mr. Gold & had premature birth abt 3 P.M.
14th still good weather. Sister mary rather better
Dr. Gold left, worked on road 3 hands & self & plow team.
Majr Brooks Jim & Jo & Andw M??ck.
1845 Nov 13th Mercury 35°. Still fine weather & has been
remarkably fine fall for business. Sister Mary better .
loaned David Bran $60- Till Jan. 7. Harrowed field S.E.
from the hosue which is much washed.
Friday 14th My 46°. fine morning, will go to Dr. Leyburns
for some inproved Bakewell Sheep
15th fine morning, returned from Lexington collected
$26.31c. from J. Judy. Spent last night with Mrs. Anderson,
sent 39 1/2 Gallons oil to Waynesboro. 30 to J. Wayt & 9 1/2 to
Mr. Withrow. Jerry brought home 11 sheep & 1 calf of Dr. Leyburn.
Sunday 16th My 36° continous good weather. Sermon by Rd. Paxton
and exhortation by Revd. Morrison both excellent.
17th My 44°. (18th) My 43°. gathering in my turnips & M. Wurtzle.
19th clean bright morning. My 46°. Smoke gone, Sister
Mary left us for B.Burg. (20th) My 48°. 21st My 52°. Fast day.
and sermon by Revd. Morrison
Saturday 22nd Clear bright morning, My 34°. No rain for 3 weeks.
23rd Cloudy morning, My 50°. sermon by Revd Kerr.
Monday 24th My 24°. clearning out race. Recd cash of J. Wayt by
Jos Much $10 yet due $10.80. (25th) Merucry 22°. (26th) My 28°
27th Cloudy morning, My 41°. filling wood house.
Friday 28th Mercury 22°. Cold windy weather for last 48 hours
Sold J. Wishrors 2 bbs flour for $5. brought home 12 Do
will go for Scottsville on Monday, nothing happening.
Saturday 29th Cold morning, My 17°. Slight skeft of snow.
Sunday 30th. Mercury 20° Sermon by Revd. Morrison. Cold day.
Monday 1st. December, Very stormy morning. sleeting
& snowing, Jerry starts for Scottsville with 12
bbls flour, Gave him cash & order 15/~ will go my self
for Lexington. Paid O.P. Baldwin $2.50 for Gazette.
Snowed abt 3 1/2 4 Inches.
1845 December 2nd Cold morning, Mercury 19° ground
covered 1 or 3 Inches with snow. Killed 10 Hogs to day
weighing 1776 3 of them abt 8 months old the bal.
18 months - Have killed this winter 22 Hogs weighing
3524 pounds. worth $176.20 - I have killed 6 hogs
this month between 8 & 9 months old averaging 148 lb-
Wednesday 3rd Hazy morning, Merucry 17°. Truly quite a winter.
spell of weathre. Have been feeding the cows for some 15
days, & have in prospect a long winter. Have one hand in
the way of cattle 8 cows, one for a beef, 6 yearling calvs, One
Bull of Dr. Leyburns stock, abt 3 months old. of hogs 2. sows, 5 Shoats
7 mos old, 13 pigs, weaned. of Horses 9 head. Sheep, 30 head.
corn scarse, Oats scarcely any, Hay abt 5 Tons, some fodder, & plenty
of straw, flour at home 9 barrels. wheat in mill 71 Bushels.
flax seed on hand abt 100 bushles. Flour worth $6. to 650 wheat
125 to 140 in Richd.
4th Fairing of after snowing 3 days this week, Snow abt 5 in
deep. Has been freezing the last 5 days. Merucry ranging from
17°. to 30°. now 8. My 22°. (5th) My 24°. clear windy & cold.
6th Very cold morning Mercury 8°.
Sunday 7th Mercury14°. Still clear & Cold, My waggon arrived last
night at 9. Jerry Some frost bitten. Sermon by Revd. Morrison.
Monday 8th My 30°. Sleeting & raining. the first rain for 5 weeks.
The last week has been one of severe cold. The mercury
rarely rising above the freezing point. The Snow still
covers the ground & it has been good sleighing for a week.
9th Cloudy warm morning, My 42°. 10th My 32°. (11th) My 20°
12th My 21°. (13th) My 21°. Mr. Jas Trimble in with us last night.
14th Sunday, Reaining & sleeting, My 34° Night, 6 In snow
15th my 38°. (16th My 30°. windy night. snow drifted spent day
at Brownsburg. (17th) Fine morning. My 24°. will attend at N.P. Church
Pd Salary 8$ contribution 5$. pd. 18th My 37°. cloudy 19th My
21°. (20th) Mercury 10°. clear & cold. Recd. cash Colo. Brown $50.
of Jno. Watt - Esqr $10. 40/100. Sunday 21st. Mercury 4°. very cold.
sermon by Revd. Morrison (22nd) My 21°. Cloudy.
1845 Decemb 23rd Mercury 16°. Clear & frosty. Leonora two
years old this day. a brisk active child, h as been
talking for 2 months. (24th) My 30°. Snowing.
Loaned Mr. Wiad $60- for five days.
Thursday 25th Merucry 30°. fine morning (26th) My 22°.
Gave servants cash 12/~ (27th) My 17°. Geo. Houston &@ [all] spent
night with us - Bright clear weather. Sister Caroline
j& childrne. Mrs. Patterson, & little ones, with J. Withrow
& Mr. Patterson spent the day with us.
Sunday 28th My 36° cloudy - sermon by Revd. MOrrison. Gave
6/~ to bible Society 29th My 34°. Killed beef, weighing 528 lb.
Tuesday 30th Merucry 40°. cousin Sarah Wayland with us (31st) My 26°
January 1st. Cloudy morning. Mercury 33°
It has pleased a kind providence to preserve
and safely keep us through another year.
and now in entering on the duties of a
new year, we would return our thanks to
an all wise & most beautiful Creator, for the
favours & blessings confered on us in time
past, and pray that through the influences
of his good spirit, we may all be enbalbed
to discharge our duties, a right in time in come.
May we O God, be guided & counseled by thee
and in all things we do, may they be done
to Divine acceptance.
The past summer will be memorable for the
great drouth which prevailed extremely over the
United States. The wheat crop was Good; Grass, corn,
& vegeatables very poor. There is now great scarcity of
corn & oats. Flour is worth in Richd $6. corn 60 to 70c.
oast 40. My stock is 9 Horses, 6 cows, 6 calves, 30 sheep
17 Hogs. supply of straw good, no oats or rye. 70 Bushs
wheat in Mill, corn, say 100 Bu few Tons Hay. 100 Bu ea potatoes &
Turnips. Grain looks well. Witner severe so far.
Thursday 1st January 1846
Pleasant morning Mercury 33°. will go to Church to
day. May God meet with us, & bless his people in
this portion of his Vineyard. a good sermon by Revd. MOrrison
paid Majr. Brooks $2.20 On a/c old irons bought at McFarlands -
Friday 2nd Fine warm morning My 47°. Good rain last night.
hired Edmuond to Jacob Judy for $20. will keep Bob myself.
a leave Jesser for John & A Crose at a hire of $30-
Saturday 3rd My 35°. Clear & windy waters quite fresh. sawing
4th My 29° Fine clear morning. Snow pretty well gone which
fell on 1st. Dec. Sermon by Revd. Morrison (5th) My 29°. went
to court, collected $25 from Mr. Geo Erklridge. 6th cloudy, My 36°.
East wind adn a very rainy disagreeable day.
7th Cloudy Merucry 37°. examination day. a good attendance
8th windy My 36°. cutting out road to McKenneys shop. paid Andrs
Patterson $1575 for flax seed, bought home 4 bls flour & offables.
9th My 35°. Jerry paid for Lexington for seed pd abt 19 Bu.
19th Mercury 27°. windy night.
Sunday 11th Fine morning, Merucry 29° windy night. sermon by
Revd. J. Horrison. pleasnat day. (12th) My 31°. a good day.
13 My 30°. 14th Mercury 22°. (15th) My 31°. 16 My 38° 17th rain My 40°
Sunday 18th My 20°. cold windy nght. Sermon by Rd Morrison.
19th My 20°. Mr. Zechariah Johnston Sr died this mornng. Aged 76 years & 1 day.
20th My 23°. Like for snow. Mr. Johnston bured to day sermon
by Mr. Morrison at the church. snowed abt 6 Inhces.
21st My 24°. wind East still cloudy & disagreeable.
Thursday 22nd Fine morning, My 32st. will spend a day at Brother
Johns, paid J.W. Culttorn $206.50 $20 again by Patteron 23rd My 10°.
spent an agreeable day in Brownsburg with Br. James
24th My 14°. Went to Lexington with James & Patterson, Took up
16 yds Jaes to crop, left with Mr. Coupton. 25th My 46°. sermon
by Revd. MOrrison. 26th My 43°. 27th My 45°. (28th) My 34°. Dined
with R. McNut 29th My 38°. 31st Returned from Waynesboro found all
well. had a muddy ride, but a pleasant Trip.
1846 February 1st. Sunday, Mercury 35°. Cloudy wind East.
2nd My 35°. 3rd Merucry 33°. Foggy morning. (4th) My 38°. clear
5th My 42°. Getting out coopers stuff, a brisk hand will
bolt out wheat stuff will make 200 barrles in a day.
& can shave from 400 to 600 staves. Fanny goes to Waynesboro
Friday 6th Merucry 38 Spent day at Lexington. 7th My 30° Snowing
snow fill abt 4 Inches deep, Thawing all day.
Sunday 8th Mercury 38°. Sermon by Revd MOrrison
9th My 22°. Making oil. 10th My 22°. Clear. 11th My 36°.
12th My 37 (13th) My 26°. clear & frosty. (14th) My 33°. cloudy with snow.
Sunday 15th Past night stormy with wind & snow 3 In deep, My 36°
sermon by Revd. Bacon of N. Yor. who spent the night
with us. Subscribed for Parleys Magazine & N. York Observer
paid cash $3.50
Monday 16th My 33°. purchased this day Kennedys Mill with
3 & 3/4 acres of land for which I am to pay
$1200. One half down on 6th Mch next & then I al in
2 years. say $350, annually. Possission(?) given this day.
17th My 29°. Fair loaned John Withrow $2 to pay for Observer. 18th My 34°.
19th my 26°. Give Miller 3/~ to pay Bob for axe. Election day for Congress
sowed 5 or six inches very inclement day, few persons at the
Election. 41 votes at Brownsb'g; 40 for McDowell. 20th My 22°
Re P of Patterson 5 1/2 & Stuart 5 1/2. Bu flax seed & of S. Patterson 12 chop (?)
Saturday 21st My 30°. windy weather. 22nd My 28° fine mornig. Sermon
by Revd Bacon. 23rd My 25°. 24th My 30° sent waggon for flax seed
to B&Armstrong. Recd 32 p Bushels. Smowed 4 Inches, 25th My 30°. 2 blly 20
fixing mill of Kennedy. & Halling saw logs to Mr. Friday
27th very cold again for 3rd time this winter, My 12°.
28th My 23°. Snowing a little Recd cash John Withrow $150.
Sunday
March 1st Stormy weather, rain & sleet. Mercury 22°
The wethaer has beenc old & bad for a week. Sermon
by Revd. Morrison, few out. 2nd very stormy morning
My 18°. still snowing & sleeting. now 3 days Esat wind & storm.
1846 March 3rd Mercury 24°. The snow lies about 6 Inches
deep with a crust. After 4 days Storm the sweather looks moore
settled.
4th Mercury 21°. bright fine morning. snow begins to thaw.
paid Andw Kennedy $600 on a/c of the Mill purchase
5th My 42°. pleasant morning. My 38°. 6th will go for Lexington to day.
pd coniftorn (?) of Dr. Crop $4.17. Recd cash Mr. Withrow $175 Do C. Wayland
Sunday 8th Mercury 48° Fine brightm oring. Snow much gone. The
last 5 days having been clear & warm. Waters brisk & ground wet.
sermon by Revd. Morrison. (9th) Still good weather, My 43° wokring on
Robinsons road all hands. 10th Still on road. My 38° went to Furnice
11th My 32°. cash Recd James McNut Esqr $43.85 (12th) My 46°. 4 Mrs Withrows
with us to spend day. hand 4 days on Robinson & Williurs road
Friday 13th My 55°. 14th My 44°. 15th fine morning. My 42°. worked on
road yesterday with 2 hands horse & cart. Jos Muck, Gregory, Patterson,
& Anw Muck Each 1 hand. (15th) Sermon Revd. Morrison.
Monday 16th skift snow last night with high wind, My 36°.
17th My 36°. 18th My 36°. paid A Kennedy $400. loaned Colo Paxton $5
19th My 47° 20th My 48°. sowed some oats on 18th. 21st My 38°.
Sunday 22nd Mercury 31°. frosty morning. sermon Revd. Morrison.
23rd My 42°. Bought of Willson Kinnedy a horse, Saddle, &
Bridle, Blanket, 2 back bands & hip straps, Trough, & nice plowing
scyth & hangings. for which I pd cash $29 & per tol.
rain in Evening. 24th My 45°. surveyed price land bought poles
George Waid in rain There is acres of it
Wednesday 25th Fine growing morning. Much rain fell,
last night. My 50° (26th) My 40°. ground very wet.
27th My 40°. (28th) Showry weather, Mercury 40°. rainy day
paid A. Kennedy infull for Mill $144.50 Cousin Edwin
with us
Sunday 29th My 38°. clean morning. Sermon by Revd. Mr. Beard
30th My 33° fine moring Recd of Cole Paxton $170 -
31st My 34. Haxy Rd Mr Beard Dined with us.
1846 February April 1st Cloady morning wind East. My 35°
Mr. Woods moves to the Mill to day.
April 2nd My 39°. Still cloudy cool weather. 3rd My 30°. Ice
4th Mercury 32°. Sowing oats. Apricots in bloom.
Sunday 5th My 34° Sermon by Fevd James Hemphreys, who is just
licinsed. pleasant day. has beeeen dry * seasonable for a week
MOnday 6th My 40°. fine moring. will go to court to day.
7th My 50°. will go to Johnstons sale to day. purchased there
117 Bushels of wheat at 65¢ & 1 threshing machine out of
order for $7 in all $83.05 due in 9 months.
Wednesday 8th My 52°. rain last night, with cloud morning, paid
Stuart & Strickler $3.75 infull fo seed. also on the 3rd Inst
paid James Compton $4.06 infull for seed.
Thursday 9th white frost. My 33°. work on road to day.
10th My 53°. Sacramental season commences to day
excellent sermon by Revd. McFarland (11th) My 52°. sermon by
Revd. McFarland. rainy morning
SUnday 12th My 58°. Still cloudy with rain lat night. Peach
trees beginning ot bloom. Sermon by Revd. Armstrong - Harris
Morrison added to the Church.
Monday 13th My 38°. Cool morning bright and clear after
seasonabl erain. 14th Mercury 30°. Frosty night high wind.
15th Mercury 50°. fine day worked on road yesterday with 7 hands
16th My 36°. Friend Trimble with us (17th) My 58°. fine morning
will go to court. Recd cash on Lucas Bond $189. (18th) My 60°. quite unwell.
Sunday 19th Mercury 60° weather warm for 3 days. My to to 78° at
noon, sermon by Revd. Beard 20th My 45°. My Millwright
Paxton, Cochron & Fur as business to day Paxton only
worked. commenced Mowing for corn
Tuesday 21st Mercury 47°. Gregory left having made 7300
Shingles. have paid him for making same. 22nd My 55°
23rd My 56°. (24th0 My 55°. will Go to Greenville to day to
Election. paid for Jimmy $1 - to Carsons Colt.
25th My 65°. cloudy 26th My 60° planted Some patches
corn & mellon seed, cucumber &@ [all]
1846 April 27th Mercury 50° Cloudy damp morning with
some reain las tnight. The past week has been very warm
and dry. The trees of Every kind has been in most beautiful
bloom & the prospect for fruit promising. we have no
preaching to day. Mr. Morrison absent in N. Carolina.
Monday 27th My 44°. (28th) My 52°. will Share some sheep to day
clipoped 29 & got 110 lb wool an average of near 4 lb.
19th My 50° good rain last night worked on road to day with 4
hands. (30th) Mercury 50°. rain to day seasonable weather.
May 1st Mercury 55°. (2nd) Mercury 50° will finish plowing for
corn to day. paid Hy Gregory $2.00 on a/c work done.
Sunday 3rd My 50° Sermon by Revd Hy. Rufner. (4th) My 48° fine
morning. will commence planting corn to day. 5th My 54°.
6th My 56°. Cousin Franklin Wayland from Misssosuri with
us - also F. Link & Colo Paxton. sold to Mr. Sprowl
my horse Rock & Little waggon for $50 payable
on 1st Jny 1847. Inclosed n Hogg Whitman &@
$20 for fish p Mr. Whitman.
Thursda 7th Merucry 56°. will finish planting corn to
day, after which will plant late potatoes.
8th My 58°. Rainy morning, wind East, heary rain.
9th My 59° Sunday (10th) My 59°. went to cold Providence &
heard Mr. Thpson preach a good sermon. Some
rain to day. ground now very wet.
Monday 11th My 52°. Engaged hawling timbers for Mill
12th My 43°. Cool morning. Willie started for school
to Mr. Payne yesterday. Wheat beginning to head
crop in many places much injured by fly.
13th My 50°. fine bright growing weather, planting melons &
potatoes
Thursday 14th My 58°. will go to Greenville for plank & waggon
pd cash for same $32. pd for Mr. Barleys umbrella 6/9
hard good rain to day. (15th) cloudy, 16th My 60°. Still
cloudy & rain like Evening very wet with high weaters
& still cloudy & unsettled
1846 May 17th. Sunday, Mercury 62°. The ground is
very wet & much washed. sermons by Revd. Saml Brown
& Morrison. pleasant day.
18th My 58°. Mediteranian wheat in bloom & looks well
wheat generally much injured by fly & worms very
bad on corn (19th) My 52°. East wind, cool. hived 2 S. Bees
Wednesday 21st Mercury 47°. Good gass weather, wheat unproving
22nd My 53°. planting late potatoes at orchard lot. 23rd My 56°.
paid A. Patterson for Albert Miller $250 to be
sent to Staunton, Present, Letcher.
24th warm morning, My 60°. Ground baked & hard, getting dry
sold 7 sheep to McKinsey for $2. Each $14.
Sunday 25th My 63°. close warm morning. sermons by Revd. Morrison.
rain. Loaned Jonny Croson $5. & Save one for S.S. Books also
gave A. Patterson $10 to remint for purchase of Books. Mr. & Mrs. Beard down
26th My 61°. clear & warm (27th) My 65°. (28th) My 68°. (29th) My 70°.
heavy rian to day Mrs. J. & W. Withrow &@ [all] spent day with us.
30th My 68°. 30th My 67°. rain amlmost every day past week, weaters
oan flush & the groun much washed. Gent muster to day at
Stuarts. (Sunday 31st) My 65°. sermon by Revd Morrison & Carter.
pleasant day. gave $1 to Education Society. Evening rain.
1846 June 1st Mercury 67°. close warm mornign will
go to court accompanied by Mrs. Jones. 2nd My 67°.
cloudy with much rain last night. Heavy washing rain
in Evening. 3rd Mercury 58°. (4th) My 68°. pd. R. McNut $3.40
5th My 67°. Storm wind & rain last night. rainy day.
6th Bright & clean, My 62°. Cherries ripe.
Sunday 7th Cool moring, My 52°. The past has been a rainy
week, the corn crop is grassy & ground been too wet to
work in. The wheat crop where good blown down &
much tangled. This crop will be short. where the ground
is thin it is nearly Eat up with fly & will be quite
a short corp in this part of the Valley.
Sermon by Revd. Morrison
Monday June 8th 1846 Meruecry 58°. cool morning
Mr. Marshall & Smith of Pennsylvania dined with us to day.
9th My 60°. rain from East. Doctrs Grauf & Leach with us.
10th My 54°. cool with ground quite wit (11th) My 60° still wet.
hawled plank from McClungs Mill. Fanny away wedning.
12th still cloudy. My 64°. (13th) My 58°. Mr. Beard with us.
Sunday 14th My 60°. Still cloudy, the weather has been went for
near a month. Sermons by Revd. Morrison
15th My 66°. Partially clear. Evening Tremendous rain for
abt 3 hours. very high waters. (16th) Foggy. My 61°. 17th My 64°.
18th My 64°. Harvest commenced. Wheat in this county generally
indifferent. Much straw brokin, having sufered greatly by the
fly.
19th My 66°. went to Furnace for Gudgions. raind heavily, 20th My 67°
Sunday 21st My 62°. fine morning. sermons by Revd. Morrison.
22nd My 50°. quite cool since (20th) will commence cuttin g
wheat to day. The harvest will not be more than half
a crop. wheat much tangled & straw broken & will be
of rather inferior quality.
23rd still quite cool. Mercury 48° (24th) My 52°. fine weathe r
25th My 54°. still good weather. (26th) My 60°. 27th My 66°. brought
home Mill spindle, water wheel finished to day & water
put on it. Misses Rains & Reamer to dinner with us.
Sunday 28th warm morning. My 68° no rain for 9 days.
light shower in Evening. Sermons by Revd. Morrison (29th) My 65°
cutting some clover, & powing corn. apples begin to ripen.
30th My 66°. July 1st Cloudy morning, My 70°. rain.
2nd Cloudy morning with East wind. My 70°. (3rd) raining, My 68°.
has been cloudy wet wewather all week wheat that is down
rotting. (Saturday 4th July)
still cloudy, Mercury 66°.
Sunday 5th My 65°. Hazy morning. Sermons by Rvd Morrison
6th went to court. Road established to Kennedy's Mill from
my land. spent night Mjr Huttons. pd for Lace &@ [all]
7th Returend home to S. Barleys. 8th My 64°. last three days
fair. finished cutting wheat. will mow in meadow to day.
1846 July 9th Merecury 65°. Fine weather for some
days. Hawling in wheat, many persons not done cutting
wheat, which is much down & injured.
10th July Friday. My 70°. expect 4 Mrs. Withrows & Mr. & Mrs. Patterson
to dinner. Mrs. Joness birth day.
Saturday 11th My 71°. went to Whitmers Mill for plant amt $4.51
Sunday 12th My 71°. close warm morning. Mercury to 90° in heat of day
for 2 days. Sermons by Revd. Morrison.
13th My 71°. Still fiar & getting dry. cutting hay & hawling
in wheat (14th) My 70°. 15th My 56°. 16th My 55°. light shower.
17th quite cool My 50°. (18th) My 56°. Evening rain
Sunday 19th very rainy morning, Mercury 55°. Sermon
by Revd. Morrison 25 persons at church.
20th FOggy morning. Mercury 56°. Engaged making hay have put
up 10 loads.
21st Mercury 58°. Still cloudy riany weahter. 22nd My 61°
23rd My 66° Still cloudy rainy weahter wet for 7 days much
grass down, and oats ready to cut. Apricots & Early apples
in fine order.
Friday 24th My 70° fine clear morning. Sacramental Season
Sermon by Revd Brown. Saturday 25th My 65°. fine day.
Sermons by Revd. S. Brown & James Humphreys.
Sunday 26th Pleasant morning. My 67°. Sermons by
Redvd. S. Brown, Humphreys & Morrison. Fine weather, and
an interseting meeting than otherwise.
27th My 66°. putting up oats which are good (28th) My 67°
29th My 65°. rain (30th) My 63°. will go to Waynesboro
with 50 Gallons oil (31st) returned from Waynesboro
sold oil for $50 trainds well. heavy rain yesterday
August 1st. Pleasant morning, My 68° (2nd) My 64°.
cloudys. Sermons by Revd. Js. Payne
Monday 3rd went to court collected from A. Linsay $256 &
cents on a/c Gabons Debt ~yt due $400. loaned Basley $20.
4th My 56°. pd Houston $460. Do Mrs. Crouse $5. Dr. W. Withrow
for cisgtern $6.40 pd Stirnet for plank $4.50
1846 August 5th My 60 fine weather for 4 days. will
sow Turnips to day. (6th) fair Still mowing.
Friday 7th Mercury 68°. Fair hot weather. 8th My 67° finished the hay.
Sunday 9th Mercury 70. Ground getting quite dry. Sermons by Revd.
Jos. Brown & Lacy. 10th My 72°. Good rain. 11th My 62°. commenced
plowing fallows 12th My 66°. 13th My 65°. fine weather for corn which
bids far to be a very heavy crop. 14th My 70°. 15th My 70°.
Sunday 16th My 70° Sermons by Revd. Hy & Jo Brown cloudy day.
17th My 72°. sent Cyrus be Mr. James to Richd Brother Mr. Betty &
Cousin Kitty Jones arrived this evening with CHarley. Waggon
gone to furnace for mettle for Davis. (18th) My 65° (19th) My 64.
20th My 68°. Peaches getting good. Nectarines nealry gone. Apples
good and in great abundance. Spaurie Lusk, Mrs Robt & Jno
Willson, Miss Davidson &@ [all] with us.
21st M 70° will go as orffence to Pr. McKerr to dya. Patterson & Cullar parted
paid out this week to J. Payne $14. to Geo Waid 7$ By cahs Jos Cutton $10
22nd Sunday My 68°. light shower last night. no preaching to dya.
23rd My 65°. a good shower. 24th East wind & rain. My 63°.
24th My 58°. (25th) My 68°. 26th My 67°. rain last night. 27th My 66°.
30th My 58°. Heavy rain & much thunder last night. Sermon on
Popery by Revd. Morrison Evening sermon by Revd. B. SMith
Gave cash to Missouri & Ohio Churches $2. 31st My 65°.
September 1st Tuesday Mercury 67°. fine day. 22nd My 69°.
3rd My 68°. 4th My 70°. 5th My 69° pd Alexander cash for brick $5.50 9 oil
pd M. Fitzgerald for digging race infull $2.00 Bought 2 cows of J. Lucas
for $19.50 Due 6th Mch 1847 (6th) My 70° Sermons Revd
Dd. Humphreys.
Monday 7th My 68° (8th) My 68° 9th My 70 (10th) My 60 Threshing
since yesterday morning. Cleared up 80 Bushels wheat
9 of Spelts & a s much oats. requires 8 or 9 hocunds (?)
to attend on Mr. Srains Machine, which will clearn
abt 100 Bushels p Day. (11th) My 61°. finished threshing
wheat have abt 250 Bushels. whih is more.
than I expcted. Mrs. Jones had a misscarriage today
now quite unwell. attended Dices sale bought 3 steers $27
1846 Sept 12th Mrs Jones something better. My 64°.
Dr. Curry still with us. Made peach butter to day 16
Gallons made from abt 40 Gallons cider, & 3 to 4 bushels
pealed peaches. Cider well boiled before the peaches were
put in. The peaches all in by sun set, & the butter
taken off at 11 P.M Shoer at 6.
Sunday 13th My 67°. fine bright morning. Mrs Jones
still qutie unwell. Pevd Saml McNut preached at Providence
to day. (14th) My 65°. Killed little Beef got of D Bear
weightin 207 lb Hide 40 lb. (15th) My 66°. Mrs. Jones better.
16th Mercury 52°. quite cool. (17th) My 50° Recd coffee 110 Sugar
260lb Loaf Do 40lb Bought of J. Merck little beef for $5. (18th) My 68°
19th My 62 have been cutting up corn for 2 days, corn good
Sunday 20th Mercury 52°. quite cool morning. Mrs
Jones again down stairs after being confined for
10 days to her bed & room, her health still feeble
21st My 65° Still cutting up corn will sow
wheat South from the house to day. 4 Bushels mediterarean
Son on abt 2 1/2 acres.
Tuesday 22rd My 52° Turning over corn ground for wehat
23rd My 53° moving Mr. Woods to Brownsburg. 24th My 59°
moving Mr. Ott to Mill. will finish cuttin gup corn
to day. will commence grinding wheat to day
25th Mercury 60° Willie will go to Waynesboro today paid
G Freen 7/6 for repairing clock. (26th) My 62°. Killed beef
weighing 325 lb. Mrs Saml. Willson died last night.
Sunday 27th Mercury 53°. Mrs Willson buried to day
Sermon by Revd Skinner, Mrs Beard to see us.
Mrs. Kinnear died this morning, at J. Stuarts in
Brownsburg. (28th) Mercury 44°. some frost.
Gathered some hill apples to day, also seek(?) no
furthers, Rolemaons, Saperb, Canadean peppers
& Nonpariel. This fruit drops Early & if
not gathered in Sept is nearly lost, all of whrich
are excellent apples. 29th My 41°. 30th My 40°
1846 Octr 1st. I am this day 49 years of age in
the enjoyment of usual health. with its attendard
blessings for which Ithank God.
Merucry 48°. Paid D. Snider $27 for 3 small
steers will average abt 400 lb Sowed to day
9 Bushels Mediteranean wheat on land got of Waid
13 bushels Sown to date. (2nd) Mercury 51°. 3rd. My 55
Have seeded to date 19 Bushels M. wheat at corn land
one bushels more will finish the field. Not very
well seeded, Ground very dry, no rain for 3 weeks.
closed Mill wrights bill to day at $587.39
mediteranean wheat sown new ground 16 bu patch 4 - 20
Sunday 4th Mercury 59°. cloudy. sermon by Revd. Mr. Beard.
5th My 46 will go to court pd. Quxir $15.15 pd Kirkpatrick
& rd cash on a/c Wright $77.60
6th My 48°. sowed 4 Bushels white wheat in fallow field
7th My 49°. roled 10 bushels white wheat got of Stoner, soaked
in brine & roled in lime. 5 bushels mixed flint &@ to soak
8th My 54°. 9th My 53°. 3 bushels sown. Finshed seeding what
this 10th Oct. have sown 40 bushels, 20 on Each side of
farm, 16 Soaked in brine & roled in lime, of white
wehat. The balance sown dry; being Mediteranean.
exept 4 Bushels sown dry, back part of field. Next 8 bu
from Stoner. Then be of mized on mil, next 2 of Stoner
the bballance miesd wheat except 2 larids(?) along the
road a finer which are of Stoners white flint. My 53°.
Sunday 11th My 39°. quite frosty. sermon by Mr. Beard. cool day.
12th My 40°. Cloudy. (13th) My 56°. rianed all night after a
long drouth of 5 weeks. Still raining, wind East. fine
rain. 14th my 42°. Put up to day abt 120 Bushels of apples.
Fruit good & abundant. (15th) My 45°. Pecd cash
Mr. Withrow 3$ paid Dr. Leach $10 for Reparing
Fannys Teeth. who warrants his work. 916th) My 45°.
17th sowed 3 1/2 Bu goose wheat on sand hill. SOld horse
Tan to Mr. Fun for $40. (18th) My 54°. sermon by Rd Morrison
19th My 31°. severe frost. (20th) My 30°. 21st My 32 will sow 4 bu M.
wheat on sand Hill. Sold 12 Bu M. What to Mrs. Ann Culton 6/~
Have sown 48 Bushels of wehat 24 Mediteranean 4 Goose & 20 white
1846 Octr 22nd Thursday. Fine Frosty morning Mercury 32°.
Making apple Butter. pd. Hoggg, Whitmer, &@ yesterday, infull.
Due Mrs. Potter for weaving $6.25, 23rd, My 34°. (24th) My 44°
Killed small beef weighting 350 lb Hide 60 lb
Sunday 25th My 37°. sermon by Revd Morrison (26th) My 36°.
27th My 48° (28th) Mercury 42°.
31st Returned from Waynesboro & Stauton, spent 7/6 & had
a very agreeable trip. attended Louisa Railroad convintion
at Staunton 2 days. Good rain to day.
Sunday 1st Novr 1846 weather mild, My 53°. no sermon to day
2nd My 56°. raining fast. 3rd My 52°. 4th My 55°. cloudy.
5th My 44°. Getting in corn. Killed Beef on 12th 410 lb & pain in Sister
Sunday 8th My 52°. stormy for 4 days with East wind & rain. have cold
9th My 55°. (10th) My 57°. 11th 60°. fine warm weather. 12th My 48°
13th My 47° (14th) My 45°. Sacramental season Dr. McFarland
preached yesterday. sermon Dr. McFarland, a good one.
Sunday 15th My 46°. Cloudy morning. Sermon Revd. McFarland
16th My 40°. Sowed 1 1/2 Bushels M. wheat in corn rows
paid Mrs. Potter on 13th $6.25 for weaving. (17th) My 38°.
18th My 41°. 19th My 44°. Cloudy. Getting in wood. rain. 20th windy My 40
21st My 38°. 22nd Sunday, My 37°. Sermon by Revd. Morrison
23rd very windy night. My 31°. 24th My 37°. 25th My 44°
Killed 10 hogs to day averaging 180 lb in all 1790
have yet 9 to kill a month iince, cold windy day
paid Mr. Echerd $8.35 for hawling 4 sacks salt 400
nails & Glass & 3/4 Ton plaster.
Thursday 26th Quite cold morning. My 20° very windy for 30 by
27th My 24. Paid A. McMarters $120. 28th My 38°. Paid B. & A.[illegible]
Sunday 29th My 60°. warm & windy. sermon by Revd. Morrison
30th My 33°.
December 1st My 35°. cloudy. will
go to Waynesboro to day to see Niece Better Wright who is
ill. 3rd Returned from Augusta foudn all well at
home. weather wet & warm. 4th My 36° went to Lexington
paid for Gazette from 1st Sept 1846 to Do 47
pd for fulling 13 yds cloth $1.30 ecd. cash of
Majr Stuart on a/c Reid $3.25.
s1846 Decembr 5th Mercury 28°. Frosty. Gathering Turnips
6th Sunday cloudy & Like for snow. Sermon by Revd. Calhoun
7th My 37°. considerable rain yesterday & last night. 8th My 44°
9th My 46°. windy night (10th) My 36 SLeeting (11th) My 35°. windy
12th My 31°.
Sunday 13th Frosty morning, My 28°. prayer Meeting at Church
14th My 30°. Cousin John E. Beard with us. 15th My 28° (16th) My 23°
our Niece H.E. Wright died of Typhoid Fever, after on illness of
near a month. one the Evening of teh 15th Just.
17th My 30°. very stormy night, snow fell some 8 or 10 Inches
wind very high from East. snowed all day over 1 foot deep.
18th My 31°. clear. (19th) My 32°. (20th) sunday, My 24°. windy cloudy & cold.
21st Monday My 32°. The country blocked up in Every direction with
snow which fell on the 17th Tis much deeper, and abt 18 In deep
pounds 1767 in all to which add 1790 killed some time
ago makes my stock of pork 3567 pounds.
Tuesday 22nd Mercury 26°. 23rd my 24° paid Shaper infull on
serun at Mill $10.25 Settled with Bryan &@. due Mr $9.04
24th My 20° Hazy. 25th My 46°. a Thaw, snow much melted last
night, winday day & night, 26th Mercury 33°. Clear & Bright
Sunday 27th Mercury 44°. sermon by Revd Morrison 28th My 48°
29th My 40°. fair weather. (30th) My 46°. warm day 31st My 50
paid Mrs. Crouse $50.
1847 January 1st
Fine warm Morning Mercury 57°. Spent the
day at Lexington accompanied by David William
My stock consists at present of 7 head of horses, 7 cows & 7
young cattle, 33 SHeep & 12 head of hogs, with a good
supply of provinder of Every kind. Stock all in good
order.
2nd Mercury 51°. very warm weather for midwinter.
Snow which fell on 17th litt gone.
1847 January 3rd Mercury 36°. Some frost after 2 weeks
warm weather. Sermon by Revd Morrison
4th My 36°. cold rin with strong East wind. 5th My 33°
6th Mercury 32°. 7th My 40°. (8th) Very cold, Mercury 2°.
windy & cold Mercury 2° James Withrow & family to dinner
with us Merucry rose to 18° fell a tnight to 12°.
9th Mercury 12°. clear & cold. paid Salaray to A. Patterson $14.50 on 14th.
Sunday 10th Mercury 32°. Cloudy & like for snow. Sermom by
Revd. Morrison. (11th) My 26°. Snowed abt 8 Inches last night.
12th My 18° Cold night 13th Still frosty My 20° 14th My 38°. cloudy
15th My 42°. Spent Jerry to Lexington with 4 B. flour 9 bu Turnips
6 Bu potatoes & 15 Bushels apples (16th) My 57°. rainy morning
Sunday 17th Fine frosty morning, My 24°. Snow gone. Sermon by
Revd. Morrison. Recd cash Mr. Brownlee uinfull for flour $3-
18th My 30° 19th My 40°. (20th) My 24° Skift of snow.
working on Willsons road for 2 days. 21st Frosty & clear My 13°
sold Mr. Brow[n]lee 1 Bbl flour $4.50, 22nd, My 10°. clear & cold.
23rd My 22°. fetting out clover seed.
Sunday 24th My 36°. sermon by Revd. Morrison (25th) My 49° paid
Colo Paxton $10. (26th) My 39°. Cloudy. spent day at Mrs. Pt. Withrows
27th My 35°. Making fence to Majr Brooks road. 28th My 19°
29th Sleeting & snowing. My 30°. killed beef 450 lb hid 68 lb
30th My 32° Sunday 31st. My 28° Fine morning. Sermon by Revd. Morrison
February 1st went to court, & done nothing as usual. My 33°. 2nd My 28
3rd My 50°. rain. 4th very cold moring. My 12°. 5th My 22°.
6th Fine morning, My 34°. Brought home sow & 6 pigs from D. Beard $5.
(drawing of a cow)
Sunday 7th My 30° Fiar & Frosty. Sermon by Rvd. Morrison
8th My 34°. (9th) My 40° 10th My 36°. little snow. (11th) My 28° Clearing
clover seed 5/~ Bu. 12th My 25°. 13th th My 26° paid Mr. A. Patterosn
$50 borrowed of him 1st Jany.
Sunday 14th My 24°. sermon by Revd. Morrison. 15th My 33°. 16th My 44°.
Sent 11 Barrles flour by Mr. Wade to Scottsville 17th My 46° 18th My 40 ° rain
paid J. Keenedy for Billys hire $2. (19th) My 40°. (23rd) returned from Lexington
Recd cash of M. Blair $50. (24th) My 23°. 25th My 33°. Little snow.
Harper down Surveying read by M Kinzys & Coopers 26th My 33°
27 Mercury 33°. Sleeting 28th My 31° cold wind sermon Rd Morrison

family more or less sick with cold, 2nd My 30°. clearr
3rd My 37°. cloudy. (4th) Mercury 35°. raining & snowing some little

5th Mercury 34°. clear, will commence plowing to day. sick list better

for Staunton tomorrow. Hired Missrs Gray & McDowell at

25 Recd cash Mr. McCormick for oil $12. 26th My 48c. pd. Patterson

Mercury 38°. 2nd My 50° will sow some oats to day

8th My 46°. spreading dung on oats. sowed flax seed 9th My 64°.
10th My 49°. paid A. Smith for J. Weir 7/6 pd. carson & Gold 5/~ seed $3.37 1/2
pd Engleman on a/c Farr $3.62 1/~ for silp 6/~ for timeber.
Sunday 11th Mercury 41°. fine morning sermon by Revd. Morrison
12th My 42°. Bright & Clear. 13th My 46°. finished sowing oats
14th My 45°. cloudy. 15th My 46°. 16th My 27°. frosty. at squire McNuts
17th My 41. Recd cash J. Judy $20 % paid Strickler & Coniry $8.56
paid James & John Buchanan infull $11.00
Sunday 18th My 32°. sermon by Revd Morrison, Gave 6/~ Educaton Sy
19th My 28°. working on road. 20th My 47° 14 pgis from 2 sows
their first littler. 21st My 60 22 Election day. My 62°. Senate Kinney 336
Congress Gray 329 Congress McDowell 229 Dorman 309 Harper 350 Gold 193 Jones 152
2nd My 63°. paid Brubeck $5. Towards flax seed 24th My 42°. cloudy
John Henry very unwell. Sunday 25th My 36°. Revd. Mn absent.
26th My 37°. very dry, cool weather. 27th My 60°. 28th my 56°. will
commence planitng corn to day & go for cogo. pd Snudar $15
29th My 62°. planted field in corn next Nutty. 1 1/2 Bu seed.
30th My 50° planting lots abt house.
May 1st My 48°. cloudy but very dry 2nd My 55° little rain.
3rd My 46°. 4th My 45°. pealing bark. 5th My 52°. 6th My 40°
7th My 43°. 8th My 50° Sacramental season 9th My 56°. a good
shower last Evening after 6 weeks dry weather. Sermon by
Revd. Saml Brown & Morrison, M. F. Wright joined church
Monday 10th Raining moderatly & now seasonable after
long ophill dry weather very little rain for last 7 weeks till now
Merucry 58°. wind east. Recd. crorn Carson by Ott $10. pd same to
McFadden for plank &@ (11th) My 60° wind still East & clody & misting 12th My 60° snowy. 13th My 56°. Clipd 34 Sheep to day have in wool
14th My 50 planting pumpkin seed & some corn in field next
Nuttys. 15th My 52°. Gent Muster, fine day.
Sunday 16th My 50° sermons by Revd. Sheilds & Morrison 17th
My 42°. cool morning. will been at School 4 days 18th My 50°.
19th My 46°. 20th My 52°. planting potatoes in new ground.
Pd. Mrs. POtter $2.20 for weaving. Do Gold & Carson for Miller 1.20
Do Do For Linene 554 planted abt 18 Bushels potaotes 21st My 52°
22nd My 63°. 23rd My 60° sprinkle of rain seron my Revd. Calhoun
24th My 59°. Seasonable. 25th My 53°. 26th My 65°. friend Brown with us.
27th My 60° cloudy working on road & hawling coal 28th My 60°
replanting corn 29th My 56° (30th) Sunday. Mercury 59°. sermon by Revd. Calhoun.
31st My 56°. will go to court collected of J. Compton $11 for flour.
June 1st My 60°. Recd. cash Brownlee $6. 2nd My 62°. again at court
done nothing of note. paid Mr. Davis $75. gave not for $57.81. on sight.
3rd Mercury 57°. finihsed repairs to mill. 4th My 60°. Recd. cash of
Bryan for ore $24.04 (5th) My 59° cloudy. 6th Sunday My 60°.
7th My54°. plowing corn 8th My 60° will go to McGrody for plank
pd Lhu note for 9 3/4 flax seed, Do McGuffin in oil for $10 bushl.
Wednesday 9th My 62°. fine bright morning, will go for Waynesboro
to day. Grains & flour now high, corn sells for 90c. to 1.12&.24
wehat $2.12 to 2.24 oats 60c. rye 6/~ prices tend upwards. very
little flour or corn on hand. The growing crop of corn looks
bad abt 4 to 5 Inches high & badly up wheat only tolerable.
11th Returned from Waynesboor, found & left fiends well. Had
a pleasnat trip & good rain last night. 13th My 60° Mr. Marrion
abest at windy cove. 14th My 58°. rain last night. will
go to Jns Mr Stuartrs to day with Mrs. Jones. By cahs Jajr Brooks
$45 (paid same to Davis $57.81 in all) By cash Mipple $10 -
of Miller 6/~ 15th My 55°. Recd. cahs for 4 Bbls flour $29- of J. Obt
16th My 58°. cloudy. 17th My 60°. 18th My 57°. 19th My 64°.
Sunday 20th June 1847. Cloudy & rain like My 66°
Sermon by Revd. Morrison. Mr. W. Alexander buried to day
21st My 55°. commence mowing clover hay which is short
22n dMy 55°. 23rd My 58°. put up 4 loads clover hay. 24th My 66°.
threshed out with 2 men & 2 girls 90 Bushels corn. will send 55 to
Scottsville on Monday.
25th Friday, My 66°. cloudy weather with but little rain
26th My 66° (27th) Sunday My 70°. sermons by Revd. Morrison 28th My 65°
waggon goes to Scottsville with 54 bushels corn. Mrs. Withrow spent day
with us. 29th My 68°. Harvest commenced. 30th My 60°. good rain
yesterday. July 1st
Mercury 55°. cool day 2nd My 58° wagon returned from Scottsville
corn worth 70 to 75c. Recd. 1 Bbl Shad & 1 sack salt $10. & 2.25 & cash $20
3rd Mercury 58°. (4th) Mercury 59° Fair fine weather
sermons by Revd. Morrison. 5 th went to court & had road
Estabished through lands JOhn Withhrow Brooks 7 Fur.
got 307 for damages 30 for Bridge & 55$ in labour to open
road - (6th) My 60°. cutting wheat with 2 cradles.
what begins to be slightly rusted.
7th Mercury 64°. cloudy. 8th still cloudy but very dry. My 68°.
will finish cutting wheat to day 9th My 66°. raining moderately
10th Fine rain & still raining, My 68°. setting out plants
for cabbage.
Sunday 11th My 68°. dark damp weather. sermons by
Revd. Morrison, 12th My 66°. growing weather. 13th plowing potatoes
& hawling in what My 69°. 14th My 70° Mowing have put up
5 loads hay to date. 15th Mercury 60° (16th0 My 61°. sowing Buck wheat
17th My 68°. Making hay & hawling in wheat 18th My 68°. sermons by
Revd. Morrison. 19th Mercury 70°. getting in wehat & hay.
Daniel patterson had his mill burnt last night
by some malisious scoundrel. with much wood
grain &@ loss some $200o to 3000$.
20th Fair, My 70° puling flax. 21st My 66°. fine rian
yesterday - Jerry goes to Richd to day
22nd My 68°. Luke & Fleming working for Me from this day
23rd My 68°. Good rain yesterday & last night. 24th My 70°
Sunday 25th My 71°. fine growing weather. sermons by
Revd. Morrison. 26th My 70°. threshed abt 85 Bu wheat
1847 July 27th Mercury 60°. rainy dark weather. Cose Albert
Waylan & Br. & mrs. Bacon with us. 28th My 50° quite cool
Took 57 Bushesl wheat to mill & put away 48 for see.
29th Mercury 57°. Cos Albert left for home (30th) My 55°.
paid J. & J. Newton $20 on a/c Dd Ott ak Squire McNutts.
Saturday 31st Mercury 60°. Engaged putting up oats have put in
Mill 150 Bushels wehat of good quality, and have foe seed
54 Bushels crop of oats light not more than 150 Bushels.
Hay crop of good quality & well put up abt 25 Tons
Sunday August 1st Mercury 67° sermon by Revd. Neville "2n My 66" 3rd My 61°. 20
Ladies & children to dinner Mr. Nuty & Withrows, Spent pleasnt
day. Wednesday 4th Mercury 61°. will get in lat of the oats
a short copr. also 3 or 4 loads hay. will sow some turnip
seed in new ground. pd P. Trotter $10 on a/c Books
5th My 60°. Jerry came home. cleaned up 1 3/4 Timothy seed
6th My 62°. East wind with some rain. (7th) My 59°. heavy rain
to day & waters high.
Sunday 8th My 60°. Foggy morning. sermons by Revd. Morrison
10th rain last night, My 72°. 11th My 66°. much rain yesterday groudn too wet
to plow for several days. (12th) My 67°. fine growing weather.
Revd. Bun Sr Smith & Family spent night with us. 13th My 65°.
Sermon by Revd Hy. Brown. Sacramental season. 14th My 64°
Sermons by Revd. White & B.M. Smith, 15th sermons By Revd. Smith and
Henry Brown, Monday 16th My 65°. Cousin Susa Wayland
Mr. and Andw Withrow with lots of childrne with us. went to
Staunton. 17th My 68°. weather still unsettled & rain like.
18th My 63°. fair fine morning, 19th My 56°. 20th My 53°. fallowing.
Presbytery in Session at River Church, Bethesda, 21st My 60°. cloudy.
Sunday 22nd Mercury 68° Cloudy with little rain, sermon
by Revd. Willson from Inida. (23rd) My 65°. cloudy damp
weather. 24th Sitll cloudy & rainy. Mr. Withrow went
home yesterday in the rain. Ground very wet.
wind East. My 60°. fine quite comfortable.
25th My 62°. Still dark weather. Cleaning off Cedar Hill
1847 August 26th Mercury 56°. fine quite agreeable for the
last week. fine bright morning. (27th) Still clear My 58°
spent day is commissioner on Coopers land 28th My 65°.
will go to Coops to day again. Finished dividing land
at Coopers between James McNutt & James Cooper
Sunday 29th My 60°. bright cool weather. sermon by
Revd. Morrison. 30th My 57°. adjourned Presbytery meet in
Lexington on a/c Revd. Hohn Skinner on this 31st Augt. My 62°. rain
September 1st
Foggy morning, My 62°. fine growing weather, fining Scran at Mill
2nd Mercury 64°. Hazy. sent by Mr. Waid 12 barrels of
flour & firkin butter to Scottsville & 10 Gallons of
oil to Wm Withrow. sowed 3 bushels of wheat to
day burined & roled inlime, in Field next Mucks
& north East. 4th My 63°. 1 Bushel wehat sowed to day
Sunday 5th My 72°. warm night, Mr. Morrison absent assisting
Revd. Carmpbell. Sally Beard with us, a good shower to day.
Monday 6th My 70°. fine morning sowed 5 1/2. bushels wehat to day
& 5 Bushels of rye which will be harrowed tomorrow
7th My 64 will sow 1 1/2. Bushels wheat to day which will
finish field next Mucks corn N.E. from house. Have
sown to date 11 Bushels wheat & 5 Bushels rye. 16 Bushels
sowed in same field in 1843 - 28 Bushels wheat & rye
8th My 70° raining a little. sowing Timothy seed on Elm
Tree field. 9th My 70°. fine moring. heavy rain at noon
finished sowing timothy seed on Elm Tree hill.
Have in Mill 14 bbls flour. sent by bills on 3 & Brownlee
7 barrles flour to Richd acnd 2 barrles due
from wheat loaned out.
10th My 53°. (11th) My 50° Sunday 12th My 57°. dark weather
13th Fine morning. My 54°. Willie again at school after an
absense of 2 weeks. 14th My 47°. quite cool. 15th My 42°°. Slight
frost, will sow to day 5 1/2 Bushels goose wheat on
Persimmon Hill. also 1 Bushels Mediteranean wheat
Thursday 16th My 46°. will sow to day 7 Bu. M. Wheat
on Persimmon Hill. Cousin Edwin with us & paid me $30.
Septr 17th My 50°. attended Miss Hannah McChesneys
wedding last Evening. upwards of 200 persons present
Mr. Winn The Spouze, quite a young man. Mr. Blakey
little son Angus died yesterday. sowed to day 4 Bushels
of wehat, which finishes Persimon hill, on
which is sown 5 1/2. Bushels Goose wheat & 12 of
Meditiranean. have sown to date 28 Bushels wheat
& 5 rye.
Saturday 18th My 50° have had fine weather for a week
cutting clover seed & Manuring hickory tree field. took out
7 loads manure, went to Church to hear Revd. Willson from
India, gave $4 to F.B. Misssions. pd Beart 11/3 for seed.
19th My 54°. fine rain last night. Sermon by Revd. Morrison
20th My 52. put up hogs to fatten on 18th. 9 in all, 3
of which are good & 6 small the latter would not now
weight over 50lb. Each one anaverage. have a good lot
of hogs at the Mill, 12 of which will weight when killed over
200 lb. sent Pevd. Payne by son Willie $2 for Books.
Tuesday 21st My 52° Cutting grass, & hauling out manure.
Red. By Jeames Willson for 3 bbls flour sold $16.75 pd for 1
Bushel Harsha Wheat 2¢. hauling 62 1/2 22nd My 48°. clearn as a bell
23rd My 52° pleasant weather. 24th went morning. My 60°.
bougth of Mr. McCLung a mare colt foaled 29th Abt
for which I have $20 cahs Hawling logs to Mill
for Hogpen heavy rain last night & to day -
25th My 55°. fine morning sold sheep to Green for 10/6 paid McGee
Hein Ab $4 on order from Bradly & Shaw his cost 30¢. paid
Jacob Larco $3 for 4 Bushels wheat.
Sunday 26th My 50°. sermons by Revd. Turner & Beard, fine
day & large congregatoin. 27th My 55°. Topping & cutting up some
corn. 28th My 64°. fine moring. will put up hog pen at
Mill. 29th My 44°. quite cool but fine weather. sowed one
bushel wheat on Cedar hill which cost me $2.64 per
bushel. (Shankar wheat) will sow to day 2 bushels
white wheat same field. 30th My 54°. will go to Revd.
Paynes Examination to day. sowed in hickory Tree
field 4 Bushels wheat to date.
1847 Octr 1st
I am this day 50 years of age, in the enjoyment of
unusual helath, for which lessing. I render thanks to
God, by whom, may I in all things be directed for
his glory, & My Eternal good. My 62°. sowed 3
bushels wheat to day. Recd. of Gordon & Skinken 130 lb sugar 8 1/2
2nd My 62°. paid Brownlee carriage on 7 Bls flour & sugar $11
Bought Mr. Wrights sale 1 Hor? 2$2 1 fork 45 rake 50. 1 edstead 59
1 Do 100 2 boxes 38. & 1 shovel & collars of Troxell 4/6 paid
same except $2.09 which is yet due (our Table $1.12 1/2
Sunday 3rd Cloudy morning, East wind, My 54°. Had an
excellent sermon by Revd. Beard. 4th Oct. My 44°. will go to
court. Finished sowing Hickory Tree field on Saturday
having sown 10 Bushels wheat on same. Have sown
to date 38 Bushels wheat & 5/~ rye. The corn crop
ripens slowly. I am now cutting up my corn.
The fall has been favourable for business with pleasant
weather & no frost to do any injury.
5th My 46°. Killed small beef weighing lb 6th My 64°
rain last night. 7th My 66°. Mr. B. Strickler with us very heavy
rain to day waters high & ground very wet Paid B.
Strickler $50 for smut mashine 8th My 55°. finished cutting
up fileld corn next Nuttys. 9th Bright morning, My 54°.
cutting little hay for calves. Sunday 10th My 53°. Sermons by
Methodist Brethren. Gave $2 to Bible cause. Friend
Brown & lady with us. 11th My 56°. getting in Hay
& clover seed. 12th My 52°. will seed in corn land
next Nuttys to day. 13th My 44°. rain last night. paid John
Robinson 716 infull for flax seed Returned James Kennedy
$90 out of $100 borrowed. 14th My 34°. heavy frost. have
been quite unwill for 3 days with cold
15th My 31°. fine frosty morning. finished sowing wheat
have sown in all 46 Bushels wheat & 5 rye
paid Mrs. Ott 20/~ for weaving 8 1/4 James ab(?) & 20 Linsey bd(?)
1847 Oct17th Mercury 39°. No preaching at N.P. to day, fine weather,
went to old Providence with Mrs Jones, 18th My 45°. cuttin g
Buckwheat. (19th) My 48°. (20th) My 50°. Cloudy. Killed small beef
2312 lb 21st My 45° working at buckwheat & Otts Kitchen.
Mary Plum Patterson killed to day by fall off a horse, an ir (?)sting
fine child about 7 years old -
22nd My 43°. 23rd My 63°. cousin Caroline Wallce & Children
leave us to day. will send Jerry with oil to Lexington
some reain, Mr. Wethers spent evening& night with us.
Sunday 24th My 48°. still cloudy with some rain sermon by
Revd. Morrison 25th) Merucry 55°. good rain last night.
26th My 44°. will go to Walkers sale to day. bought over 100 Bushels
corn at 35 cts (27th) cool morning, My 34°. pd cash to Mr. Brorden
for plank $5. (28th) My 30°. quite frosty will go for corn at Shanks
29th My 26°. Brought home yesterday 97 1/2 Bushels corn & today
26 Bushels Brownlee got 45 Bushels in all 168 1/2 Bu
at 35 cents $58.97. due in 9 months from 26th. Sacramental
season at N.P. sermon by Revd. McFarland. 30th My 30°
Sunday 31st. My 34°. sermon by Revd. McFalrand.
Nov. 1st
Monday 1st My 45° will go to court. paid 60 cents insurance
Tickit, loaned James Withrow $10 to pay Taxes. Settled with
J.M. Willion Recd. cash $1.45. Do. A. Withrow $25. for oil sold
Rdcd J.D. Davidson $6 for apples. paid out to A.P. Davis on
a/c note cash &@ to amt $231 - yet due from 1st Octr
$125. paid Wright silvermsith 3.50 for repairing watch
3rd fine morning. My 42°. paid James Kennedy $253 for
hawling Mutter Cheese &@ office, and $10. infull for cash
borrowed. (4th) My 52°. hawling out chip manure (5th) My 50°.
hawling in corn. 6th My 40°. 7th My 44°. cloudy. No preaching at Providence
Oevd. Morrison assisting Dr. McFarland. attended preaching at Fairfield
8th My 50°. will take 43 bushels buch wheat to Mill & fix Bridge
9th My 64°. hawling wood (10th) My 61°. gathering turnips & putting up cabbage
11th My 42°. 12th My 35°. sent waggon to Lexington with load of
Turnips, Bought of John Stuart Negro Man Madison,
aged 36 at $500. Saturday 13th My 48°. cloudy & rain at night
fixed location of New Schoool School house, on Mucks
Land, & bought of him 1/8 of an acre of groudn to
build on
Sunday Novr. 14th My 48°. sermon by Revd Morrison.
Monday 15th My 44°. started Jerry to Scottsville with 10 Bbls flour, gave him $ [illegible]
16th My 34°. putting up corn 17th My 38°. killed 2 hogs at Mill
weighing 130 & 150 each 280. put up 50 Bushels Turnips &
sent 16 Bushels to the Mill 2/~ for James Kennedy 3 1/2
for Mr. Farr 2 for Fitzjerald & 8 1/2. Ths. Gregory - 17th My 50° will
go for Waynesboro' to day. 20th My 28° paid Newton infull $20.12 1/2
paid Javir Snider $5. on a/c of cogs, infull A. Patterson
present & Lindwick jr. Recd. from Scottsville 1/2 Ton plaster & sack salt
Sunday 21st My 30°. sermon by Revd. Morrison. 22nd My 32° rain
23rd My 48° cloudy & went. 24th Still raining & waters very high My 55
25th again fair, Mercury 43°. 26th My 32°. Hewing school house logs
27th My 25° very frosty. Bridgs n the North River taken & much
damage done by the flood of the 24th.

body.p: Sunday 28th My 33°. sermon by Revd. Morrison, 29th My 24°. 30th My 34°.
December 1st. Cloudy morning, My 24 Rcd 34 Bu flax seed
of B&Armstrong, paid Davis $2.50 rain. 2nd My 44°. 3rd My 45°.
spent day at Mill fixing boling cloth. Sent off bbl flour by
Mr. Paxtor for Pichd. Killed 3 hogs Weighing 638lb 4th My 32°.
Sunday 5th My 35°. fine morning. Sermon from Rvd. Morrison
6th went to court, Recd. cash A. Withrow for oil & Turnips $5.
My 33°. Tuesday 7th My 23°. 8th My 28°. 9th My 44°. Foggy. 10th My 60°
11th My 60° rain for last 3 days. fixing gates abt. burn yard.
Sunday 12th hMy 45°. rain. 13th My 62°. still raining. 14th My 32°. Billy 34
11th My 30°. Killed 8 hogs at Mill 1542 lb 17th snowed
last night about 1 foot deep (18th) My 20°. Clear
19th My 34. sermon by Revd. Morrison. roads very bad, & a small
congregation. 20th My 30°. 21st My 30 Snowing.
22nd My 24°. unpleasant morning 23rd My 17° Clear
24th My 38°. James Morrison buried to day.
Saturday 25th Decr.
Dull cloudy Morning, My 37°. ground mostly
covered with now. Which 17t. 26th My 10° sermon by Red Morrison.
27th My 10° 28th My 22° (29th) My 28°. 30th My 37°. 31st My 48°.
Snow neary gone groudn very we. tquite foggy paid Mrs.
Crouse $5 paid P. Trotter $10 -
1848 January 1st
Mercury 55°. The morning is warm, The last 3 days
have been soft rainy & foggy. With much mud &
bad raods. We ?niter up on the new year with good
health. for which I praise God, who has Ever been
good unto us, anu I pray for his guidance & direction,
may we do nothing contrary to his will, and may
we grow in the knowledge of his ways, and so live
as to merit a continuance of his Divine favour.
My stick is in good condition, with a good supply
of necessary food. & consists of 5 horses & 2 colts, 12
cows & heifers, 8 calves 33 Sheep, 2 brood sows & 14 pigs
1 White bull & 6 hogs to kill, My family consists of wife & self 3
children ^neice & 9 Servants.
Sunday 2nd Merucry 40° Strong wind. sermon by Revd. Morrison.
3rd My 30°. went to court. 4th My 38°. spent day Brownsburg, paid Dr.
Gold $85- pd Salary 13$, 6th My 37°. old Mrs. White & Ladies to see us yesterday
7th My 28°. 8th My 30°. paid Mary. G. Johnston $3. Tuition & Dr. Gold $1.88.
Sunday 9th My 37°. windy. sermon by Revd. Morrison (10th) My 12°. will kill
hogs to day. weighing of 6 not quite year old 876 lb an average of 146
have put up this year 3340 lb pork & a have beef to kill. Sent
Mrs. Anne White one hog 142 lb (11th) My 13°. (12th) My 28° put 9 loads manure
on hill above the road. hawled 18 saw logs to Mill. 13th My 32°. 14th
My 33 15th My 46°. Clearning up colver seed, put away in the nough
abt 7 to 8 Bu seed, loaded waggon with 10 Bbls flour & 45
gallons oil for Waynesboro & Scottsville, paid S. Patterson
by son $350
Sunday 16th My 45° rain last night. sermon by Revd. Morrison.
17 Started waggon to Scottsville sent 10 Bbls flour & 1 Bbl oil
to waynesboro - to WW 29 1/2 Gallons, gave Jerry $2.50. My 37° 18th My 32
19th My 20° (20th) My 22°. fixing cart, 21st My 27° repairing fence at
spring house & putting up gate. 22nd My 36°. Still repairing fence
Jerry returned from Scottsville, sold My four for $6.06 1/4
cahs. Brought home 2 Tuns plaster & 10 1/4 flax seed from
Waynesboor. Sunday 23rd My 30°. fine weather for 8
days. sermon by Revd. Morrison, Large congregation, 24th M y52°
corn fodder fed out. 25th My 34° 26th My 42°. rainy 27th Foggy My 46°
28th My 37°. clear. 29th My 36° very windy. 30th My 35° sermon by Revd. Morrison
31st Mercury 28°. Mr. Withrow of Waynesboro to see us with cousin
